dervis-irab:11-11.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الإفك): the most extreme form of lying; it is also said to be a slander (buhtān) of which you are unaware until it takes you by surprise. Its root is al-ifk, which is "turning over", because it is speech turned away (maʾfūk) from its proper face.
(كِبْرَهُ): the kibr of a thing, with kasra on the kāf and sukūn on the bāʾ, is its greater part. Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm said, mentioning a woman:
تنام عن كبر شأنها فاذا ... قامت رويدا تكاد تنغرف
(She sleeps through the greater part of her affairs, and when she rises, slowly, she almost bends and breaks.)
[Translator's note: the source prints the poet's name as «فيس», an evident misprint for «قيس» (Qays).]

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ جاؤُ بِالْإِفْكِ عُصْبَةٌ مِنْكُمْ): the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), beginning the narration of the story of the slander (al-ifk). It runs over eighteen verses that will follow in sequence, and it concerns ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her; she was a righteous woman deserving of praise and commendation, so whoever accused her of evil has, as it were, overturned and obliterated the facts. إنّ and its noun; the clause جاءوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; بالإفك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) جاءوا; عصبة is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; منكم is a naʿt (adjective) of عصبة, i.e. from among the believers, even if only outwardly — for ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, one of those who plunged into the talk of the slander, was among the chief hypocrites. The clause لا تحسبوه is resumptive; the address here is to the Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿĀʾisha and Ṣafwān, as consolation for them. The story of the slander will come in the section on benefits.
(لا تَحْسَبُوهُ شَرًّا لَكُمْ بَلْ هُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ): لا is jussive-governing; تحسبوه is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm); the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); شرا is the second direct object; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شرّ; بل is a conjunction indicating digression (iḍrāb); هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and خير the khabar; لكم is attached to خير. The aspect of good in it is the reward that the one afflicted by the trial obtains, then the manifestation of honour and the shining clarity of the truth through the revelation of eighteen verses declaring your innocence, and the dire threat of punishment against whoever plunged into it with evil intent and purpose.
(لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ مَا اكْتَسَبَ مِنَ الْإِثْمِ): لكل امرئ is a fronted khabar; منهم is a naʿt of امرئ; ما is a relative noun, a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause اكتسب is its ṣila; من الإثم is attached to اكتسب.
(وَالَّذِي تَوَلَّى كِبْرَهُ مِنْهُمْ لَهُ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; الذي is a mubtadaʾ; the clause تولى كبره is the ṣila, i.e. he went to extremes in it, magnified matters and embellished them out of the evil of his inner self and the wickedness of his heart; منهم is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). He is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, the hypocrite. له is a fronted khabar and عذاب عظيم a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of الذي.

* Benefits:
The account of the slander (ḥadīth al-ifk):
It is reported in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, in the words of ʿĀʾisha, who said: "I was with the Prophet ﷺ on an expedition after the ḥijāb had been revealed. He finished it and returned, and drew near to Medina, and one night he gave the order to set off. I walked away, attended to my need, and came back towards the camel saddle, and behold, my necklace had broken. So I went back to look for it, and they lifted my howdah thinking I was in it — the women were light then; they ate only a small amount (al-ʿulqa) of food. I found my necklace and came after they had moved off, so I sat down in the halting place where I had been, thinking the people would miss me and come back for me. My eyes overcame me and I slept. Ṣafwān had stopped for rest (ʿarrasa) behind the army, then set off early in the night (adlaja) after resting, travelled from there, and reached my halting place in the morning. He saw the dark shape of a sleeping person and recognised me when he saw me, for he used to see me before the ḥijāb. I woke up at his saying 'We belong to Allah and to Him we return' (istirjāʿ) when he recognised me, and I covered my face. By Allah, he did not speak a single word to me, nor did I hear any word from him other than his istirjāʿ, when he made his mount kneel and stepped on its foreleg. Then he set off leading the mount with me on it until we reached the army after they had halted, entering the fierce heat (mūghirīn) at high noon. Then those who perished on my account perished, and the one who took the greater part of it upon himself among them was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl."
Explanation of the rare words of the ḥadīth:
1- His words "on an expedition": it is said to be the expedition of al-Muraysīʿ, also called the expedition of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq. It took place in the fourth year, or it is said in the sixth. Its cause was that news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that Banū al-Muṣṭaliq were gathering to fight him, their leader being al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Ḍirār, the father of Juwayriya, wife of the Prophet ﷺ. When he heard of this he went out against them until he met them at one of their watering places called al-Muraysīʿ, in the direction of Qudayd towards the coast. They fought, and Allah routed Banū al-Muṣṭaliq and gave His Messenger power over their children, women and wealth, which he took as spoil (afāʾahā) and then returned to them.
2- "They ate al-ʿulqa": with ḍamma on the ʿayn and sukūn on the lām, a small amount of food.
3- Ṣafwān: he is the eminent Companion Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal al-Sulamī.
4- ʿArrasa: with shadda and fatḥa on the rāʾ, i.e. he halted by night to rest; it is specific to the last part of the night.
5- Adlaja: with shadda and fatḥa on the dāl, he travelled from the beginning of the night.
6- "At his istirjāʿ": i.e. at his saying "We belong to Allah and to Him we return."
7- "I covered my face with my jilbāb": i.e. I covered it with the wrap (al-mulāʾa).
8- "And stepped on its foreleg": i.e. he put his foot on its knee.
9- Mūghirīn: in al-Qāmūs: al-waghra is intense heat; waghrat al-hājira (on the pattern of waʿada) [the midday heat became intense], and awgharū means they entered into it. Al-waghr, also with a vowelled ghayn: rancour, malice, enmity and blazing with rage; waghira ṣadruhu (on the patterns of waʿada and wajila), waghran and wagharan with vowelling. And in al-Miṣbāḥ: "And he fell into a desert land, he came to be in it."
The Orientalists' version: The account of the slander has occupied the Orientalists, who have cast it in various versions. We present here, for information, the version of Brockelmann, the German Orientalist, author of the book "History of the Islamic Peoples". The following is the text of its Arabic translation:
"During the year 627 the Prophet also undertook several campaigns against some of the Bedouin tribes, and in one of them he went so far as to come near Mecca. These raids were safe to an extent that allowed him to take two of his wives along. It happened once that his favourite wife ʿĀʾisha bint Abī Bakr — who was then fourteen years old — lost her necklace, so she went out in the evening to look for it, and the caravans of the raiders left without her. She did not return to the camp until the following day, accompanied by a young man whom she had known before. Doubt about ʿĀʾisha's faithfulness crept into the Prophet's soul, so he sent her back to her parents' house. But Allah soon declared her innocent, after a single month, in one of the verses revealed to the Prophet, adding at the same time that any accusation of a woman of marital infidelity not supported by four eyewitnesses is considered a calumny or slander (qadhf) for which its author deserves a hundred lashes. ʿAlī, the Prophet's son-in-law, was one of ʿĀʾisha's adversaries who urged him to divorce her, and there is no doubt that the roots of the hostility ʿĀʾisha revealed towards ʿAlī after he became caliph over the Muslims go back to this period. Be that as it may, this incident of the necklace did not have the slightest effect on the social status of women in Islam, as is supposed: the veil adopted by married women was an ancient Arab custom, and the Prophet had imposed it before this incident for other reasons. In fact the veil did not prevent women in the Jāhiliyya, and in Islam too until the Umayyad era, from appearing among people with much freedom and from influencing Arab society, at times notably. The institution of the harem, whose rules the Abbasids laid down on the model of the Christian-Byzantine pattern, is alone responsible for the decline of women in the East."
Brockelmann's version, for all its precision, is not free of flaws, errors and a hidden prejudice which its author tries to conceal but which insists on showing itself; among this is his saying "so he sent her back to her parents' house".
[Translator's note: the source prints «ففاتتها فوافل الغزاة», evidently a misprint for «قوافل» (caravans); translated accordingly.]
The return to Medina and the clamour of talk:
Let us return to ʿĀʾisha's own account in the remainder of the aforementioned ḥadīth. She said:
"When we arrived in Medina I fell ill for a month, while the people were busily spreading what the people of the slander said, and I was unaware of any of it. What made me uneasy in my illness was that I did not see from the Messenger of Allah the kindness I used to see from him when I was ill; the Messenger of Allah would only come in, greet, and then say: 'How is that one of yours (tīkum)?' That made me uneasy, but I was not aware of the evil until I went out after I had convalesced, and Umm Misṭaḥ went out with me towards al-Manāṣiʿ. Then we came back, and Umm Misṭaḥ stumbled over her wrap and said: 'May Misṭaḥ perish!'
I said: 'What an evil thing you have said! Do you revile a man who was present at Badr?'
She said: 'O you (hantāh), have you not heard what he said?'
I said: 'And what did he say?'
So she told me what the people of the slander said, and my illness increased upon my illness. When I returned to my house I asked permission to go to my parents, wanting to make sure of the news from them, and he gave me permission.
My mother said: 'Take it easy, for by Allah, seldom has there been a beautiful woman with a man who loves her and who has co-wives, but that they have said much against her.'
I said: 'Glory be to Allah! Have people really been talking about this?' I wept that night until morning; my tears did not cease and I could not get any sleep.
The Messenger of Allah called ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Usāma ibn Zayd, consulting them about parting from his wife. As for Usāma ibn Zayd, he advised the Messenger of Allah according to what he knew of the innocence of his family and of the love he felt in himself for them, and said to the Messenger of Allah: 'They are your family, and we know nothing but good.'
As for ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: 'Allah has not constrained you, and there are many women besides her; and if you ask the maidservant she will tell you the truth.'
So the Messenger of Allah called Barīra and asked her: 'Have you seen anything from ʿĀʾisha that makes you suspicious?' She said: 'By Him who sent you with the truth, I have never seen anything in her that I could fault her with, more than that she is a young girl who falls asleep beside her family's dough, and the domestic goat comes and eats it.'
.. I wept that day of mine; my tears did not cease and I could not get any sleep. Then I wept the following night; my tears did not cease and I could not get any sleep, and my parents thought that the weeping would split my liver.
While we were in that state, the Messenger of Allah came in, greeted, then sat down, recited the testimony of faith, and then said: 'To proceed, O ʿĀʾisha: such-and-such has reached me about you. If you are innocent, Allah will declare your innocence; and if you have committed a sin, then seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him, for when a servant confesses a sin and then repents, Allah turns to him in forgiveness.'
When the Messenger of Allah had finished his words, my tears dried up until I could not feel a single drop of them. I said to my father: 'Answer the Messenger of Allah for me.' He said: 'By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah.' So I said to my mother: 'Answer for me.' She said: 'Likewise, by Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah.' I said — and I was a young girl who did not recite much of the Qur'an —:
'By Allah, I know that you have heard this until it has settled in your souls and you have believed it. If I tell you that I am innocent, you will not believe me; and if I confess something to you — and Allah knows that I am innocent — you would believe me. By Allah, I find no example for me and you except as the father of Yūsuf said: «فصبر جميل والله المستعان على ما تصفون» (so patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe).'
Then I turned over and lay down on my bed. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah had not left his seat, nor had anyone of the household gone out, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down revelation upon His Prophet, and there seized him what used to seize him of intense distress (al-buraḥāʾ) at revelation, so that drops of sweat like pearls would roll down from him on a winter day.
When it was lifted from the Messenger of Allah, and he was laughing, the first word he spoke was to say: 'Rejoice, O ʿĀʾisha! As for Allah, He has declared you innocent.'
My mother said to me: 'Get up and go to him.'
I said: 'By Allah, I will not get up to go to him, and I will praise none but Allah, who sent down my innocence.'
Abū Bakr used to spend on Misṭaḥ because of his kinship with him and his poverty, and he swore never to spend anything on him again. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: «ولا يأتل أولو الفضل منكم والسعة أن يؤتوا أولي القربى ... إلى قوله: ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم» (And let not those of virtue and means among you swear not to give to relatives … up to His words: Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?)
Abū Bakr said: 'By Allah, I do love that Allah should forgive me,' and he restored to Misṭaḥ the maintenance he used to spend on him."
What relates to this ḥadīth will come in the remaining verses.
[Translator's note: the source text reads «كما قال أبو يوسف» ("as Abū Yūsuf said"), i.e. the father of Yūsuf (Jacob); rendered "the father of Yūsuf". It also reads «فنأكله» ("and we eat it") in Barīra's words, evidently for «فتأكله» ("and it eats it"); translated as the latter.]

dervis-irab:12-15.t:
* I'rab:
(لَوْلا إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتُ بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ خَيْراً): resumptive (mustaʾnaf) speech, beginning the rebuke of those who plunged into the slander and reproaching them for the rumours they spread. Nine successive rebukes will follow, and this is the first rebuke. لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) containing the sense of rebuke and reproach, which is frequent in the language when it enters upon a verb, as in His words, Exalted is He, «لولا أخرتني». إذ is an adverb of past time attached to (mutaʿalliq) ظنّ; the clause سمعتموه is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it. ظن المؤمنون is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); والمؤمنات is conjoined (maʿṭūf); بأنفسهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خيرا; خيرا is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(وَقالُوا هذا إِفْكٌ مُبِينٌ): وقالوا is conjoined to ظنّ; هذا is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and إفك the khabar (predicate); مبين is a naʿt (adjective); the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The discussion of the splendid shift of person (iltifāt) in this verse will follow.
(لَوْلا جاؤُ عَلَيْهِ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَداءَ فَإِذْ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِالشُّهَداءِ): لولا is a second particle of urging, and this is the second rebuke. جاءوا is a verb and its agent; عليه is attached to شهداء; بأربعة is attached to جاءوا; شهداء is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). فإذ: the fāʾ is a conjunction and إذ is an adverb of past time attached to الكاذبون; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and jussive government; يأتوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it; بالشهداء is attached to يأتوا.
[Translator's note: the source writes «حرف تخصيص» ("particle of specification"), evidently a misprint for «تحضيض» (urging), and «فاذا» for the Qur'anic «فإذ»; translated as intended. Earlier it also writes «تسعه» for «تسعة».]
(فَأُولئِكَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْكاذِبُونَ): the fāʾ is the connective (rābiṭa); أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; عند الله is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. in His judgement; هم is a second mubtadaʾ or a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); الكاذبون is the khabar of أولئك or the khabar of هم, and [in the latter case] the clause is the khabar of أولئك.
(وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ): the wāw is a conjunction; لولا is a particle of non-occurrence due to occurrence (imtināʿ li-wujūd); فضل الله is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is necessarily omitted. This is the third rebuke. عليكم is attached to فضل; ورحمته is conjoined to فضل; في الدنيا is attached to an omitted ḥāl; والآخرة is conjoined to الدنيا.
(لَمَسَّكُمْ فِيما أَفَضْتُمْ فِيهِ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ): the lām occurs in the apodosis of لولا; مسّكم is a verb and its direct object, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. فيما is attached to مسّكم; the clause أفضتم فيه is the ṣila (relative clause), and «ما» denotes the talk of the slander; ifāḍa is rushing headlong and plunging in. It is also valid for ما to be maṣdariyya, i.e. "would have touched you because of your rushing and plunging into the slander". فيه is attached to أفضتم; عذاب is the agent and عظيم a naʿt.
(إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ بِأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ وَتَقُولُونَ بِأَفْواهِكُمْ ما لَيْسَ لَكُمْ بِهِ عِلْمٌ): this is the fourth rebuke. إذ is an adverb attached to مسّكم or to أفضتم; تلقّونه is an imperfect verb from which one of its two tāʾs has been dropped; it is nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the agent and the hāʾ the direct object. Talaqqī, talaqquf and talaqqun are close in meaning [receiving, catching, picking up]. The clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it, and the meaning is: some of you relate it from others. بألسنتكم is attached to تلقّونه; وتقولون is conjoined to تلقّونه; بأفواهكم is attached to تقولون; ما is the object of تقولون; the clause ليس is the ṣila of the relative; ليس is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; لكم is its khabar; به is attached to علم; علم is the noun of ليس.
(وَتَحْسَبُونَهُ هَيِّناً وَهُوَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَظِيمٌ): وتحسبونه is an imperfect verb, its agent and its first direct object; هينا is the second direct object; the wāw is circumstantial (li-l-ḥāl); هو is a mubtadaʾ; عند الله is a ḥāl; عظيم is the khabar of هو; and the clause is circumstantial.

* Rhetoric:
1- Expressing others by "selves":
Expressing others by "selves" (al-anfus) contains the most far-reaching of subtle points and those richest in lofty meanings. First, it calls upon the believers to mutual sympathy and to directing the reproach at oneself rather than mentioning [the other] with evil; that is more conducive to winning him over and to treating him on the basis of loyalty and closeness. This is done by portraying him as one who has started to slander himself and accuse himself of an indecency that is not in him. It is related that Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī said to his wife: "Do you not see what people are saying?" She said to him: "If you were in Ṣafwān's place, would you betray the sanctity of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with something evil?" He said: "No." She said: "And if I were in ʿĀʾisha's place I would not betray him; and Ṣafwān is better than you, and ʿĀʾisha is better than me."
This is entirely correct. ʿĀʾisha's innocence is clear and self-evidently understood by every fair-minded person who understands that a woman like ʿĀʾisha would not expose herself to such suspicion in front of an army, in broad daylight, and without necessity, with a man of the Muslims who feared what a Muslim fears in such a situation — the anger of the Prophet, the anger of the Muslims and the anger of Allah. That is a trait above which a woman lesser than ʿĀʾisha in lineage, rank, character and pride would raise herself, so how much more so she, in her well-known position! This is what is understood from expressing other believers by "the self": it moved the wife of Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī to put her husband in Ṣafwān's place and herself in ʿĀʾisha's place, and then to affirm innocence and trustworthiness for herself and her husband, so that it is affirmed for Ṣafwān and ʿĀʾisha a fortiori.
Second, it is possible that the expression "selves" is literal, the intent being to bind the one who thinks ill to [the same judgement on] himself, because he did not take account of the impulses and restraints of faith in the case of others, while he found and took account of them in the case of himself, and claimed innocence for himself before knowing [the facts], by the judgement of whim, not the judgement of guidance.
2- Shift of person (iltifāt):
In the speech there is a turn from the second person to the third, and from the pronoun to the overt noun. The course of the discourse would be to say «لولا إذ سمعتموه ظننتم بأنفسكم خيرا وقلتم». Eloquence required this iltifāt and the turn from pronoun to overt noun only for emphasis in the reproach, and so that the word "faith" would be stated explicitly, indicating that sharing in it requires that no believing man believe against his brother, nor any believing woman against her sister, the words of a fault-finder or a detractor. This is what the Prophet ﷺ did, and it would have befitted the others to follow his example: he heard talk being chewed over among the hypocrites and spreading to the Muslims, indeed to the closest of his own kin — talk heard by a man like ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, in the goodness of his nature, who then saw no harm in divorce, women being many. The Prophet heard that suspicious talk and neither accepted it without proof nor rejected it without proof. It was for him either to visit his sick wife or to keep his distance from her for a while; so he visited her, with such gentleness and fairness as forbade him to confront her, in her illness, with what was stirring in his noble soul, and with such displeasure and watchful waiting as forbade him to meet her as he used to meet her when the soul was entirely clear. He kept asking after her as one who has a reproach to make, waiting for her to recover and for the proof to come to him, so that he would be wholly severe or wholly merciful. The clamour of people did not hurry him, in this painful situation, into acting at once on what jealous honour (al-ḥamiyya) requires and what chivalry (al-murūʾa) requires.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy and Misṭaḥ:
If it is said that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy was one of those with tribal backing (ʿaṣabiyya) whose weight is reckoned with and whose outbursts are guarded against, what is to be said of Misṭaḥ, who was Abū Bakr's dependant and protégé, eating from his wealth? What saved him from displeasure and punishment and guaranteed him the continuance of kindness and support, were it not for the magnanimity of the noble Prophet, the magnanimity of Abū Bakr and the magnanimity of the Qur'an?
[Translator's note: the source reads «التي بحسب حسابها», evidently for «التي يُحسب حسابها» ("whose weight is reckoned with"); translated accordingly.]
3- Hyperbole (al-mubālagha):
The discussion of a similar expression, «تقولون بأفواهكم», has preceded: speech is only by the mouth, so what is the point of mentioning mouths? We repeat that here it is for emphasis and for the insinuation that one may speak glibly and pronounce with the glibness of one who is certain and knowing — which is more severe and more decisive. Its meaning is that a thing known exists with its knowledge in the heart, and the tongue expresses it; but this slander is nothing but speech that runs on your tongues and circulates in your mouths, without expressing any knowledge of it in the heart.

dervis-irab:16-20.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْلا إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ قُلْتُمْ ما يَكُونُ لَنا أَنْ نَتَكَلَّمَ بِهذا): this is the fifth rebuke. لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) and reproach; إذ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) قلتم; i.e. it behoved you, at the mere first hearing, to say: "It is not fitting for us to speak of this," and to say "Glory be to You". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: How is it permissible to separate between لولا and قلتم by the adverb? I say: adverbs have a special status, namely that they are treated, in relation to things, as the things themselves, because things occur in them and are never separated from them; hence latitude is allowed with them that is not allowed with others." Abū Ḥayyān replied to him, saying: "This gives the false impression that this is specific to the adverb, whereas it applies to the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) as well: you say لولا زيدا ضربت (why did you not strike Zayd) and لولا عمرا قتلت (why did you not kill ʿAmr)." The secret of fronting the adverb will come in the section on rhetoric.
The clause سمعتموه is what the adverb is put in construct with; the clause قلتم has no grammatical position because it is initial (ibtidāʾiyya); ما is negative; يكون is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb; لنا is its fronted khabar (predicate); أن and what follows it is its postponed noun; بهذا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نتكلم; سبحانك is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the clause سبحانك is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because its meaning is wonder; the meaning is: why did you not say "It is not fitting for us to speak of this", in the state of being amazed at this strange, astonishing matter.
[Translator's note: in this paraphrase the source has «أن تتكلم», evidently for «أن نتكلم» as in the verse; translated accordingly.]
(سُبْحانَكَ هذا بُهْتانٌ عَظِيمٌ): هذا is the mubtadaʾ (subject), بهتان the khabar, and عظيم a naʿt (adjective).
(يَعِظُكُمُ اللَّهُ أَنْ تَعُودُوا لِمِثْلِهِ أَبَداً إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): this is the sixth rebuke. يعظكم has been made to include (ḍummina) the meaning of a verb made transitive by عن, then the preposition was omitted, i.e. He forbids you from returning. It is an imperfect verb and its direct object; الله is the fāʿil (agent); أن and what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition; لمثله is attached to تعودوا; أبدا is an adverb of time, also attached to تعودوا. It is also said that there is no implied inclusion (taḍmīn) in the meaning of يعظكم, and that أن and what follows it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "out of aversion to your returning". إن is conditional; كنتم is kāna and its noun; مؤمنين is its khabar; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. if you are believers, then do not return to the like of it.
(وَيُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآياتِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; يبين الله is a verb and its agent; لكم is attached to يبين; الآيات is the direct object; الله is a mubtadaʾ and عليم حكيم are two khabars of الله.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحِبُّونَ أَنْ تَشِيعَ الْفاحِشَةُ فِي الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): a resumptive clause, brought to present the seventh rebuke. إنّ and its noun; the clause يحبون is the ṣila (relative clause); أن and what follows it is the object of يحبون; الفاحشة is the agent [of تشيع]; في الذين آمنوا is attached to تشيع.
(لَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ): لهم is a fronted khabar and عذاب a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ; أليم is a naʿt; في الدنيا والآخرة is a second naʿt. In this world it was established by the ḥadd (prescribed penalty) for slander (qadhf); the details of this will come in the section on benefits. الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يعلم its khabar; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا تعلمون its khabar.
(وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ رَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ): this is the eighth rebuke. لولا is of non-occurrence (imtināʿiyya); فضل الله عليكم is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is necessarily omitted; ورحمته is conjoined to فضل; وأن الله رءوف رحيم is conjoined to فضل الله; and the apodosis of لولا is omitted, i.e. He would have hastened punishment upon you.

* Benefits:
It is established that the Prophet ﷺ applied the ḥadd to the four slanderers: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, Ḥassān ibn Thābit, Misṭaḥ and Ḥamna bint Jaḥsh. Ṣafwān lay in wait for Ḥassān ibn Thābit and struck him with the sword, and blinded him; about this he says:
توّق ذباب السيف عني فإنني ... غلام إذا هو جيت لست بشاعر
ولكنني أحمي حماي وأتقى ... من الباهت الرامي البريء الظواهر
(Take the edge of the sword from me, for I am a young man who, when lampooned, is no poet; but I defend what is mine to protect, and I take revenge on the slanderer who accuses the outwardly innocent.)
Ḥassān ibn Thābit recited verses in which he praised the Mother of the Believers ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and cleared her of what had been attributed to her, among them:
حصان رزان ما تزنّ بريبة ... وتصبح غرثى من لحوم الغوافل
حليلة خير الناس دينا ومنصبا ... نبيّ الهدى والمكرمات الفواضل
عقيلة حي من لؤي بن غالب ... كرام المساعي مجدها غير زائل
مهذّبة قد طيب الله جنيها ... وطهرها من كل شين وباطل
فإن كان ما بلغت عني قلته ... فلا رفعت سوطي إليّ أناملي
وكيف وودي ما حييت ونصرتي ... بآل رسول الله زين المحافل
له رتب عال على الناس فضلها ... تقاصر عنها سورة المتطاول
(Chaste and composed, she is not suspected of any doubtful matter, and she rises hungry for the flesh of heedless women [i.e. she backbites no one]; wife of the best of people in religion and rank, the Prophet of guidance and of abundant noble deeds; the noblest lady of a clan of Luʾayy ibn Ghālib, noble in their endeavours, whose glory does not fade; refined — Allah has made her nature good and purified her of every blemish and falsehood. If I said what you were told I said, then may my fingers never lift my whip to me. How could that be, when my love as long as I live and my support are for the family of the Messenger of Allah, the adornment of assemblies? He has ranks high above people in excellence, beneath which the ascent of the aspirant falls short.)
[Translator's note: the source prints these verses with the line divisions displaced (e.g. «غير / زائل», «الم / حافل»); they are given here in their proper verse order without changing any word. «هو جيت» is a print-split of «هوجيت».]

* Rhetoric:
1- Fronting and postponing (al-taqdīm wa-l-taʾkhīr):
In His words, Exalted is He, «وَلَوْلا إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ قُلْتُمْ …», the adverb is fronted for an important benefit: to show that it was obligatory upon them to refrain from speaking of the slander as soon as they first heard it. Since mentioning the time was more important, fronting was required. ʿAbd al-Qāhir has a discussion in Dalāʾil al-Iʿjāz on fronting and postponing, in which he says: the chapter of fronting and postponing is one of the chapters through which the excellence of speech appears, by which one style rises above another, and through which the inimitability of the Qur'an becomes manifest.
2- The secret of the exclamation:
In the word of wonder «سبحانك» there is a wonderful secret: originally Allah is glorified upon seeing something wondrous among His works; then it became frequent until it was used upon anything that is wondered at.

dervis-irab:45-49.t:
* I'rab:
(وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ ماءٍ) A resumptive statement set out to explain the kinds of creation. (الله) is the mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause (خلق) is the khabar (predicate), (كل دابة) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (من ماء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلق), i.e. a drop of sperm, according to what is most common. (فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى بَطْنِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى رِجْلَيْنِ) The fāʾ is ramifying (tafrīʿiyya); (منهم) is a fronted khabar and (من) a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause (يمشي) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (على بطنه) is attached to (يمشي); and (ومنهم من يمشي على رجلين) is conjoined to what precedes it. (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى أَرْبَعٍ) Conjoined. The secret of using (من) for non-rational beings will come in the section on rhetoric.
(يَخْلُقُ اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) (يخلق الله ما يشاء): an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila. (إن الله): inna and its noun; (على كل شيء) is attached to (قدير), and (قدير) is the khabar of inna. (لَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنا آياتٍ مُبَيِّناتٍ وَاللَّهُ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) A resumptive statement set out to mention His signs, Glorified is He, by way of iltifāt (shift of address), as will come in the section on rhetoric. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification; (أنزلنا) is a verb and its agent; (آيات) is the mafʿūl bihi and (مبينات) an adjective. (الله) is the mubtadaʾ and the clause (يهدي) its khabar; (من) is the mafʿūl bihi and the clause (يشاء) the ṣila; (إلى صراط) is attached to (يهدي) and (مستقيم) is an adjective. (وَيَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَبِالرَّسُولِ وَأَطَعْنا) A resumptive statement set out to begin explaining the state of the hypocrites. (يقولون) is a nominative imperfect verb and its agent; the clause (آمنا) is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); (آمنا) is a verb and its agent; (بالله) is attached to (آمنا); (وبالرسول) is conjoined to (بالله), and (أطعنا) is conjoined to (آمنا). (ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّى فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ وَما أُولئِكَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ) (ثم) is a conjunction; (يتولى) is a nominative imperfect verb; (فريق) is the fāʿil; (منهم) is an adjective, and (من بعد ذلك) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the demonstrative refers to the aforementioned saying. The wāw is circumstantial; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative; (أولئك) is a demonstrative in the position of nominative as the noun of (ما); the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (المؤمنين) is genitive in form, accusative in position, as the khabar of (ما); the clause is a ḥāl. (وَإِذا دُعُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; (دعوا) is a passive past verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (إلى الله) is attached to (دعوا) and (رسوله) is conjoined to (الله). What is meant is the Messenger of Allah, as when you say «أعجبني زيد وكرمه» ("Zayd and his generosity pleased me"), meaning the generosity of Zayd. The lām is of cause (taʿlīl); (يحكم) is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied (muḍmara) «أن» after the lām of cause, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (دعوا); (بينهم) is an adverb attached to (يحكم). (إِذا فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ) (إذا) is the idhā of surprise (fujāʾiyya); it has taken the place of the fāʾ in linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) to its condition, which is the first (إذا). (فريق) is the mubtadaʾ; (منهم) is an adjective, and it is what has permitted beginning with it [an indefinite noun]; and (معرضون) is the khabar of (فريق). (وَإِنْ يَكُنْ لَهُمُ الْحَقُّ يَأْتُوا إِلَيْهِ مُذْعِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (يكن) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (لهم) is the fronted khabar of (يكن) and (الحق) its postponed noun; (يأتوا) is the apodosis; (إليه) is attached to (يأتوا), and it may be attached to (مذعنين). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is better, because of its link being placed before it and its indicating restriction (ikhtiṣāṣ). The meaning is that, because they know that with you there is nothing but the bitter truth and pure justice, they turn away from being judged before you when the right is against them, lest you wrest it from their grasp by your judging against them in favour of their opponents; but if they have a right established against an opponent, they hurry to you and are satisfied with nothing but your judgement, so that you may take for them what is owed to them by the opponent." (مذعنين) is a ḥāl. Al-Zajjāj said: al-idhʿān is hastening with obedience. In al-Qāmūs: "adhʿana lahu: he submitted, humbled himself, acknowledged, and hastened in obedience."

* Rhetoric:
1- Ṣiḥḥat al-tafsīr (sound explication):
In His saying, Exalted is He, «وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ» (the verse), there is a remarkable rhetorical device which its scholars have called "ṣiḥḥat al-tafsīr" (sound explication), and which Ibn al-Athīr in al-Mathal al-Sāʾir called "proportion between meanings" (al-tanāsub bayn al-maʿānī). Its definition is that the speaker brings at the beginning of his speech a meaning whose import cannot be grasped on its own: either it is general (mujmal) and needs detailing, or it is ambiguous and needs orientation, or it is open to more than one sense, so that what is meant needs a preference that is only attained by explaining and clarifying it. The explication occurs in various ways: sometimes it comes after a condition or after something that carries the sense of a condition, sometimes after a preposition and its genitive noun, and at times after a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the explication. The verse before us is of the kind that occurs after a preposition and its genitive noun. For He, Glorified is He, mentioned the highest genus first, saying «كل دابة» ("every creature"), thereby encompassing all kinds of whatever creeps and moves; then He explicated this highest genus by the intermediate genera and the species, saying «فمنهم» and «ومنهم», observing order: He placed first what walks without an instrument [i.e. without limbs], because the verse was set out to show His power, to extol Himself by it and to make the listeners marvel at it, and what walks without an instrument is more wondrous than what walks with an instrument; therefore eloquence required placing it first. Then He placed second the better and then the better: He mentioned what walks on two legs, namely man and the bird — because of the perfection of man's creation, the complete beauty of his form and shape and the beauty of his proportion, which requires that he be singled out with reason; and because of the wonder of flight in the air that the bird possesses, indicating the utmost lightness and the extreme of subtlety despite the density in it. Third He placed what walks on four, because it is the best and strongest of the dumb animals, giving it precedence over the insects that walk on more than four. Thus all the categories were encompassed, and the order was excellent, in addition to [the devices of] order (tartīb), allusion (ishāra), consequence (irdāf) and beautiful arrangement (ḥusn al-nasaq).
The author of al-ʿUmda defined it as the poet giving the full explanation of what he began with in general terms, and he said this rarely comes except in more than one verse. He illustrated it with two verses of al-Farazdaq:
لقد جئت قوما لو لجأت إليهم ... طريد دم أو حاملا ثقل مغرم
لألفيت منهم معطيا ومطاعنا ... وراءك شزرا بالوشيح المقوم
(You have come to a people such that, had you taken refuge with them as one pursued for blood or bearing the weight of a debt, you would have found among them one who gives and one who thrusts sidelong behind you with the straightened spear.)
The author of al-ʿUmda stipulated that it be free of faulty enjambment (sūʾ al-taḍmīn). He said: Among the good examples of tafsīr is the saying of Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī — also attributed to ʿUtayba ibn Mirdās:
متى ما يجىء يوما إلى المال وارثي ... يجد جمع كف غير ملأى ولا صفر
يجد فرسا مثل العنان وصارما ... حساما إذا ما هزّ لم يرض لهبر
وأسمر خطيا كأن كعوبه ... نوى القسب قد أربى ذراعا على العشر
(Whenever my heir comes one day to my wealth, he will find a handful neither full nor empty: he will find a horse like the rein [in obedience], and a sharp cutting sword which, when brandished, is not content [merely] to slice flesh, and a brown Khaṭṭī spear whose joints are like the stones of dry dates, exceeding ten cubits by one.)
This is the sound tafsīr free of enjambment, because he did not make his words depend on «لو» as al-Farazdaq did. Similar is the saying of ʿUrwa ibn al-Ward:
وإن امرأ يرجو تراثي وإن ما ... يصير له منه غدا لقليل
ومالي مال غير درع ومغفر ... وأبيض من ماء الحديد صقيل
وأسمر خطيّ القناة مثقّف ... وأجرد عريان السراة طويل
(A man who hopes for my inheritance — what will come to him of it tomorrow is little indeed; I have no wealth but a coat of mail and a helmet, a white polished [sword] of tempered iron, a brown, straightened Khaṭṭī spear, and a short-haired, tall horse with a bare back.)
Thus they recited it, with iqwāʾ (variation of the rhyme vowel); and it may be put in the nominative by way of severance (qaṭʿ) and an implied element, as though he said: "it is polished" (هو صقيل), or said: "and I have a white one of tempered iron", meaning his sword.
And Dhū al-Rumma said, in tafsīr:
وليل كجلباب العروس ادّرعته ... بأربعة والشخص في العين واحد
أحمّ علافيّ وأبيض صارم ... وأعيس مهري وأروع ماجد
(Many a night like a bride's gown I have clothed myself in with four, while the figure to the eye was one: a dark ʿIlāfī [saddle], a white cutting [sword], a whitish Mahrī camel, and a noble, glorious man.)
[Translator's note: the source prints «أحمّ علا فيّ» as separate words; the usual reading is «أحمّ علافيّ», a saddle attributed to ʿIlāf; translated per the usual reading.]
So he explicated what the four are. He put them in the nominative on the condition of the implied element I mentioned before, as though it were said to him: "What are the four whose figure to the eye is one?" and he said: such and such and such.
The author of al-ʿUmda went on citing examples of tafsīr until he said:
"Among tafsīr is that in which the greater is explicated by the lesser, namely where the summary comes after the explanation, such as the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib [al-Mutanabbī]:
من مبلغ الأعراب أني بعدها ... جالست رسطاليس والاسكندرا
ومللت نحر عشارها فأضافني ... من ينحر البدر النضار لمن قرى
وسمعت بطيلموس دارس كتبه ... متملكا مبتديا متحضرا
ولقيت كل الفاضلين كأنما ... رد الإله نفوسهم والأعصرا
نسقوا لنا نسق الحساب مقدما ... وأتى فذلك إذ أتيت مؤخرا
(Who will tell the Bedouins that after it I sat with Aristotle and Alexander; that I grew weary of slaughtering their pregnant she-camels, and was hosted by one who slaughters purses of pure gold for those he entertains; that I heard Ptolemy studying his books, a king, a Bedouin and a townsman at once; and that I met all the virtuous, as if God had returned their souls and their ages. They were arranged for us like the items of an account placed first, and the total came last when you came.)
His saying «نسقوا لنا نسق الحساب مقدما» (the verse) is a charming tafsīr, rarely equalled in people's poetry." Further, al-Wāḥidī said in explaining the last verse: "The virtuous of all time were gathered for us and passed in succession, preceding you in existence; then when you came after them, there was in you of virtue what there was in them — like an account, whose details are mentioned and then those details are added up and at the end of the account is written 'the total is such and such' (fa-dhālika kadhā wa-kadhā), so that the sum gathers what was mentioned in the details. Likewise, there is gathered in you what was scattered among them of virtues, knowledge and wisdom."
Abū al-Ṭayyib also said, in commendable tafsīr:
إن كوتبوا أو لقوا أو حوربوا وجدوا ... في الخط واللفظ والهيجاء فرسانا
(If they are written to, or met, or fought, they are found to be knights in script, in speech, and in battle.)
He explicated and matched each kind with what befits it, without fronting or postponement. Among sweet tafsīr is the saying of Kushājim, whose name is Maḥmūd ibn al-Ḥusayn:
في فمها مسك ومشمولة ... صرف ومنظوم من الدّر
فالمسك للنكهة والخمر للر ... يقة واللؤلؤ للثغر
(In her mouth are musk, pure cool wine, and strung pearls: the musk is for the breath, the wine for the saliva, and the pearls for the teeth.)
And beautiful is the saying of Ibn Hāniʾ al-Andalusī:
المدنفات من البرية كلها ... جسمي وطرف بابليّ أحور
والمشرقات النيرات ثلاثة ... الشمس والقمر المنير وجعفر
(The love-sick among all creation are my body and a dark-eyed Babylonian glance; and the shining luminaries are three: the sun, the bright moon, and Jaʿfar.)
2- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr):
He made «ماء» indefinite in His saying «من ماء», and made it definite in His saying «وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي», because the purpose of the verse here is to show that from one single thing different things have come into being by [His] power, whose details He mentioned in the verses of al-Nūr and al-Raʿd; while the purpose in the verse of «اقترب» [i.e. Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ] is that He created the things that agree in the genus of life from the genus of water with its different kinds, so He mentioned it definite to include its different kinds.
3- Metaphor (al-istiʿāra):
The metaphor is in His saying «فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه»: He called crawling on the belly "walking" by way of implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), just as they say of a matter that continues: "this matter has walked (proceeded)", and it is said: "so-and-so, no matter walks (proceeds) for him."
4- Predominance (al-taghlīb):
In His saying «من يمشي على بطنه ومن يمشي على أربع» there is taghlīb (giving the rational precedence) of the rational over the other, of which many parallels have passed. For since the non-rational was mixed with the rational in the subdivision by «من» and «كل دابة», expressing it with «من» was more fitting for the harmony of wording.
It is said that «من» was applied to the non-rational because it was mixed with the rational. It is also possible that «من» is an indefinite noun described by the clause after it, the implied sense being: "among them is a kind that walks on its belly, a kind that walks on two legs and a kind that walks on four", in the manner of «ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف». Ibn Hishām said: In «من» it is permissible that it be an indefinite noun described by the clause after it, the implied sense being: "and among people are people who worship Allah."

dervis-irab:21-26.t:
* Vocabulary:
(خُطُواتِ): plural of khuṭwa, with fatḥa or ḍamma on the khāʾ and sukūn on the ṭāʾ. Every word on the pattern fiʿl (with kasra on the fāʾ) or faʿl (with fatḥa on the fāʾ) [or fuʿl] with sukūn on the middle radical may, when we want to give it a sound feminine plural, take vowel harmony (itbāʿ), fatḥa, or sukūn [on the middle radical]; so we say for khuṭwa: khuṭuwāt, khuṭawāt and khuṭwāt.
[Translator's note: the source text has lost its vowel marks here, so the patterns and the three plural forms appear identical in the Arabic («فعل … فعل», «خطوات وخطوات وخطوات»); they are rendered according to the evident intent.]
(زَكى): he was purified of defilement.
(يَأْتَلِ): in al-Mukhtār: "Ālā, yuʾlī, īlāʾ: he swore; taʾallā and iʾtalā are like it. I say: and from it is His saying, Exalted is He, «وَلا يَأْتَلِ أُولُوا الْفَضْلِ مِنْكُمْ». Al-aliyya is the oath, and its plural is alāyā." It is also said to come from their saying mā alawtu juhdan, when you have held nothing back.
(الْغافِلاتِ): those with sound breasts and pure hearts, in whom there is no cunning or guile, because they have not experienced affairs nor weighed situations, so they do not perceive what experienced, knowing women perceive. [The poet] said:
ولقد لهوت بطفلة ميالة ... بلهاء تطلعني على أسرارها
(I have amused myself with a soft, swaying, guileless woman who lets me into her secrets.)
Lahawtu: I diverted myself and played. Ṭafla, with fatḥa: a soft, tender woman; one says imraʾa ṭaflat al-anāmil, i.e. with soft, tender fingertips. Mayyāla: swaggering. Balhāʾ: heedless, with no guile or cunning in her, which is why she lets me into her inmost thoughts.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُواتِ الشَّيْطانِ): this is the ninth and last rebuke. لا is prohibitive; تتبعوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; خطوات الشيطان is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(وَمَنْ يَتَّبِعْ خُطُواتِ الشَّيْطانِ فَإِنَّهُ يَأْمُرُ بِالْفَحْشاءِ وَالْمُنْكَرِ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); يتبع is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); خطوات الشيطان is the direct object; the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it is a nominal clause; إنّ and its noun, and the clause يأمر بالفحشاء والمنكر is its khabar (predicate). The pronoun in إنه refers to Satan or to the one who follows, and the first is more apparent.
(وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ ما زَكى مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَداً): لولا is of non-occurrence (imtināʿiyya), and its i'rab has preceded. ما is negative; زكى is a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he", referring to Allah; منكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of أحد; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; أحد is genitive in form and accusative in position as the direct object; أبدا is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) زكى.
[Translator's note: the source makes the agent of زكى Allah and أحد its object, i.e. reading زكى in the sense of "purified"; translated as written.]
(وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ يُزَكِّي مَنْ يَشاءُ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; لكنّ and its noun, and the clause يزكي is its khabar; من يشاء is the object of يزكي; الله is a mubtadaʾ, سميع a first khabar and عليم a second khabar, i.e. He, Glorified is He, hears their words and knows their intentions.
(وَلا يَأْتَلِ أُولُوا الْفَضْلِ مِنْكُمْ وَالسَّعَةِ أَنْ يُؤْتُوا أُولِي الْقُرْبى وَالْمَساكِينَ وَالْمُهاجِرِينَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): the cause of revelation of this verse has been discussed at length, and that it was revealed concerning Misṭaḥ ibn Uthātha (with ḍamma or fatḥa on the hamza).
لا is prohibitive; يأتل is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا; أولو is the agent, treated like the sound masculine plural; الفضل is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); منكم is a ḥāl; والسعة is conjoined to الفضل. أن يؤتوا: أن and what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition, with the omission of negative لا, the implied form being "that they will not give" (ʿalā an lā yuʾtū); أولي القربى is the object, and what follows is conjoined to it.
(وَلْيَعْفُوا وَلْيَصْفَحُوا أَلا تُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction and the lām is the lām of command; يعفوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām of command; وليصفحوا is conjoined. The hamza is interrogative and لا negative; تحبون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); أن and what follows it is the object of تحبون; الله is the agent; لكم is attached to يغفر; الله is a mubtadaʾ, غفور a first khabar and رحيم a second khabar.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ الْمُحْصَناتِ الْغافِلاتِ الْمُؤْمِناتِ لُعِنُوا فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ): resumptive speech, brought to upbraid those who plunged into the slander, to threaten them severely and to reproach them eloquently. إنّ and its noun; the clause يرمون المحصنات is the ṣila (relative clause); المحصنات is the direct object; الغافلات المؤمنات are conjoined to المحصنات; the clause لعنوا is the khabar of إنّ; في الدنيا والآخرة is attached to لعنوا; لهم is a fronted khabar, عذاب a postponed mubtadaʾ, and عظيم a naʿt.
(يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَلْسِنَتُهُمْ وَأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُمْ بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): the adverb is attached to the [notion of] settled existence (al-istiqrār) to which «ولهم» is attached; it may also be attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun), namely عذاب, because latitude is allowed with adverbs that is not allowed with others. The clause تشهد is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it; عليهم is attached to تشهد; ألسنتهم is the agent; أيديهم وأرجلهم are conjoined to ألسنتهم; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تشهد; the clause كانوا has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila — and you may make ما maṣdariyya; كان and its noun, and the clause يعملون is its khabar. Parallels to it have passed.
(يَوْمَئِذٍ يُوَفِّيهِمُ اللَّهُ دِينَهُمُ الْحَقَّ): the adverb is attached to يعملون or to يوفيهم. The discussion of the annexation of إذ to the adverb and the tanwīn that attaches to إذ has preceded. يوفيهم الله is an imperfect verb, its direct object and its agent; دينهم is the second direct object; الحق is a naʿt of دينهم. What is meant by their true "dīn" is their due recompense; and in the ḥadīth: «كما تدين تدان» (as you deal, so you will be dealt with).
(وَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ الْمُبِينُ): ويعلمون is conjoined to يوفيهم; أنّ and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يعلمون; هو is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; الحق is the khabar of أنّ or the khabar of هو, the nominal clause [in the latter case] being the khabar of أنّ; المبين is a naʿt.
(الْخَبِيثاتُ لِلْخَبِيثِينَ وَالْخَبِيثُونَ لِلْخَبِيثاتِ وَالطَّيِّباتُ لِلطَّيِّبِينَ وَالطَّيِّبُونَ لِلطَّيِّباتِ): resumptive speech, brought to set out Allah's practice (sunna) in His creation: that He drives each kind to its own kind, and that every bird alights with its like. الخبيثات is a mubtadaʾ and للخبيثين its khabar, and what follows is conjoined to it. The meaning of this will come in the section on rhetoric.
(أُولئِكَ مُبَرَّؤُنَ مِمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the good; more on this meaning will come in the section on rhetoric. مبرءون is the khabar of أولئك; مما is attached to مبرءون because it is a passive participle; the clause يقولون is the ṣila; لهم is a fronted khabar and مغفرة a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being a second khabar of أولئك; ورزق كريم is conjoined to it.

* Rhetoric:
1- Rational (cognitive) metaphor (al-majāz al-ʿaqlī) in the testimony of the hands and feet; it has been discussed in full before.
2- By المحصنات He intended generality, even though the discourse is about ʿĀʾisha. The purpose of mentioning them generally is to threaten whoever assailed ʿĀʾisha in the most forceful way: if this is the threat against one who slanders any individual believing woman, then what of the threat against one who fell into slandering their lady! Moreover, making the threat (al-waʿd) general is more forceful and decisive than making it specific. For this reason Zulaykhā generalised when she said «ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا إلا أن يسجن أو عذاب أليم» (What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your wife but that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment?): she generalised while meaning Yūsuf, to intimidate him and stir alarm.
[Translator's note: the source writes «تعميم الوعد» ("the promise"), where the context indicates «الوعيد» (the threat); translated as "threat" with the source word given.]
3- It is possible that by الخبيثات women are meant and by الخبيثين men, so that the speech runs on its literal sense; and it may be that the words from which the slander was fashioned are meant, so that the speech is figurative by explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya).

dervis-irab:27-29.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتاً غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ حَتَّى تَسْتَأْنِسُوا وَتُسَلِّمُوا عَلى أَهْلِها): resumptive (mustaʾnaf) speech, brought to set out what follows from the mixing of men with women and their entering upon them at the times of their privacy. لا is prohibitive; تدخلوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; بيوتا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa), which has been discussed before; غير بيوتكم is a naʿt (adjective) of بيوتا; حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; تستأنسوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى. The meaning of al-istiʾnās is asking permission (al-istiʾdhān), by way of metonymy (kināya); the details of this will come in the section on rhetoric. تسلموا is conjoined to تستأنسوا; على أهلها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) تسلموا.
(ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ): ذلكم is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and خير the khabar (predicate); لكم is attached to خير; لعلّ and its noun, and the clause تذكرون is the khabar of لعلّ. The clause ذلكم is resumptive, and the clause لعلكم تذكرون is a ḥāl (circumstantial) giving the reason for an omitted verb, i.e. "He has sent this down to you, hoping that you will take heed."
(فَإِنْ لَمْ تَجِدُوا فِيها أَحَداً فَلا تَدْخُلُوها حَتَّى يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ): the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive government; تجدوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by لم; فيها is attached to تجدوا; أحدا is the direct object. فلا تدخلوها: the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); لا is prohibitive; تدخلوها is an imperfect verb, jussive by prohibitive لا; حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; يؤذن is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after حتى; يؤذن is passive, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); لكم is attached to يؤذن.
(وَإِنْ قِيلَ لَكُمُ ارْجِعُوا فَارْجِعُوا هُوَ أَزْكى لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; قيل لكم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause ارجعوا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). فارجعوا: the fāʾ connects the apodosis because it is a request (ṭalabī). هو is a mubtadaʾ and أزكى لكم the khabar, and the clause is resumptive. والله: the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; بما تعملون is attached to عليم; عليم is the khabar of الله.
(لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُناحٌ أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتاً غَيْرَ مَسْكُونَةٍ فِيها مَتاعٌ لَكُمْ): ليس is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; عليكم is the fronted khabar of ليس and جناح its postponed noun; أن and what follows it is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in your entering", and the preposition with its genitive noun is a naʿt of جناح. بيوتا is a direct object by extension; غير مسكونة is a naʿt of بيوتا; فيها is a fronted khabar and متاع لكم a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being a second naʿt of بيوتا.
(وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما تُبْدُونَ وَما تَكْتُمُونَ): والله: the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يعلم its khabar; ما is the direct object; the clause تبدون is the ṣila (relative clause); وما تكتمون is conjoined to ما تبدون.

* Rhetoric:
1- Metonymy (kināya) in His words تستأنسوا: its original meaning is al-istiʾnās, which is the opposite of feeling estranged (al-istīḥāsh), because one who knocks at another's door does not know whether he will be given permission or not, so he is hesitant, his heart fluttering, ill at ease — or like one ill at ease, because the situation is hidden from him. When he is given permission to enter he becomes at ease, and his hesitation and the fluttering of his heart leave him. The remote meaning of it is intended here, namely asking permission.
2- Al-irdāf (implication by a consequent): it has preceded that this is when the speaker intends a meaning and does not express it by the word coined for it, nor by an allusive word indicating many meanings, but by a word that follows on (ridf) the specific meaning and is consequent upon it, close to the word for the specific meaning as the rider behind is close to the one in front. It is clear that this kind of istiʾnās follows on permission, so it was put in place of permission. It may also be from istiʾnās in the sense of seeking information and discovering, from anasa al-shayʾ, when one sees it plainly uncovered; on this the meaning would be "until you inquire and discover the situation, whether your entry is wanted or not". The first view is the clear one. The secret of the figurative usage in it, and of turning to it from the literal expression, is to make the addressees desirous of asking permission through an intermediary [expression]. More discussion of asking permission will come in the section on benefits.

* Benefits:
In al-Qurṭubī: the cause of revelation of this verse, as al-Ṭabarānī and others related from ʿAdī ibn Thābit, is that a woman of the Anṣār said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am in my house in a state in which I do not like anyone to see me, neither father nor child, and the father comes and enters upon me, and a man of my family keeps entering upon me while I am in that state." So this verse was revealed. Abū Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the inns and dwellings on the roads of Syria in which there is no inhabitant?" So Allah sent down «ليس عليكم جناح ...» (There is no blame upon you …) — the verse.
From Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī: he came to the door of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and said: "Peace be upon you; may I enter?" He said it three times, then went back and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: asking permission is three times." A man asked permission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "May I come in (aʾalij)?" So he ﷺ said to a woman called Rawḍa: "Go to this man and teach him, for he does not know how to ask permission. Tell him to say: 'Peace be upon you; may I enter?'" The man heard it and said it, and he said: "Enter."
In the Jāhiliyya, when a man of them entered a house other than his own, he would say: "Be greeted in the morning, be greeted in the evening," and then enter, and perhaps he would find the man with his wife under one blanket. So Allah prevented that and taught what is better and more seemly.
As for the houses that Allah excepted, they are the uninhabited ones, such as hostels, the endowed lodges (al-rubuṭ al-musabbala), the shops of traders, and the buildings built for lodging, storing goods and sheltering from heat and cold. It is also said: the houses of merchants and their shops in the markets, which one enters to buy and sell.

dervis-irab:50-53.t:
* I'rab:
(أَفِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ أَمِ ارْتابُوا) A resumptive statement set out to divide the matter of their turning away from his judgement, when the right is against them, between their being sick of heart, hypocrites; or in doubt about the matter of his prophethood; or fearing that he would deal unjustly with them — given their knowledge of his state. The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī), by which intensification is made sometimes in blame and sometimes in praise; here it is of the first kind. (في قلوبهم) is a fronted khabar (predicate) and (مرض) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). (أم) is a conjunction meaning (بل), so it is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) am; (ارتابوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent). (أَمْ يَخافُونَ أَنْ يَحِيفَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَرَسُولُهُ بَلْ أُولئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ) (أم يخافون) is conjoined to what preceded; (أن يحيف) is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (يخافون). Al-ḥayf is inclining and injustice in judging. (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (هم) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a second mubtadaʾ; (الظالمون) is the khabar of (هم), and the clause is the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ — or [(الظالمون) is] the khabar of (أولئك). (إِنَّما كانَ قَوْلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذا دُعُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ)
(إنما) is the restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle; (كان) is a defective past verb; (قول) is the fronted khabar of kāna and (المؤمنين) the muḍāf ilayhi. Its accusative has been preferred because whenever two definite nouns come together, the better course is to make the more deeply definite of them [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off here in the source; the intended completion is presumably "the noun (ism) of kāna"; the interpreted maṣdar «أن يقولوا» is the more definite]. But Sībawayh did not distinguish between them, and further discussion will come in the section on benefits. (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; the clause (دعوا) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (إلى الله) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (دعوا) and (رسوله) is conjoined to (الله). The lām is of cause (taʿlīl); (يحكم) is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām of cause; (بينهم) is an adverb attached to (يحكم). Al-Zamakhsharī made the fāʿil of (يحكم) refer back to the maṣdar, since its meaning is "so that judgement may be done between them." (أَنْ يَقُولُوا سَمِعْنا وَأَطَعْنا وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ) (أن) and what falls within its scope are the noun of kāna; the clause (سمعنا) is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl), and (أطعنا) is conjoined to (سمعنا). The wāw is a conjunction; (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (هم) is a pronoun of separation or a second mubtadaʾ; and (المفلحون) is the khabar of (هم) or the khabar of (أولئك). This has preceded shortly.
(وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَخْشَ اللَّهَ وَيَتَّقْهِ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفائِزُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; (من) is a conditional noun that makes jussive, a mubtadaʾ; (يطع) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he"; (رسوله) is conjoined to (الله); (يتقه) is conjoined to (يطع), [read] with the hāʾ vowelless or with kasra, and with lengthening (ishbāʿ) or without it. The fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (أولئك هم الفائزون) has been discussed often before. (وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ لَئِنْ أَمَرْتَهُمْ)
A resumptive statement relating the saying of the hypocrites to the Messenger of Allah: "Wherever you are, we will be with you; if you go out, we will go out; if you stay, we will stay; and if you command us to jihad, we will strive." (أقسموا) is a past verb and the wāw its fāʿil; (بالله) is attached to (أقسموا); (جهد أيمانهم) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) — further discussion of it will come in the section on rhetoric — or a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being "striving" (mujtahidīn). Al-Zamakhsharī mixed the two views and made them one. (لئن): the lām is the one that paves the way for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam) and (إن) is conditional; (أمرتهم) is a verb, its agent and its direct object. (لَيَخْرُجُنَّ قُلْ لا تُقْسِمُوا طاعَةٌ مَعْرُوفَةٌ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ)
The lām falls in the answer to the oath; (يخرجن) is a nominative imperfect verb, the nūn [of the indicative] having been dropped because of the succession of like letters; the wāw is the fāʿil and the nūn is for emphasis. The verb was not made indeclinable because the nūn is not directly attached to it. (قل) is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; (لا) is prohibitive and (تقسموا) is an imperfect verb made jussive by (لا). (طاعة) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "your matter", i.e. your matter which is required of you is a known obedience, recognised, not doubted. It may also be parsed as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "a known obedience is more fitting for you and better than these false oaths." (معروفة) is an adjective. The clause (إن الله) gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) for what preceded; inna and its noun, (خبير) the khabar, (بما) attached to (خبير), and the clause (تعملون) is the ṣila (relative clause).

* Rhetoric:
1- Metaphor (al-istiʿāra):
جهد أيمانكم [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «جهد أيمانهم»]: a word borrowed from "jahada nafsahu" — when he brought his soul to the utmost of its capacity. He borrowed it for oaths. Its origin is "he swore by Allah, exerting the oath an exertion" (aqsama billāhi yajhadu al-yamīna jahdan); the verb was omitted and the maṣdar was placed first, put in its place, annexed to the object, as in «ضرب الرقاب». If you make it a ḥāl, you make it interpreted as an active participle, i.e. "exerting" (jāhidīn).
2- Ṣiḥḥat al-taqsīm (sound division):
In His saying, Exalted is He, «أَفِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ» (the verse) there is a device called ṣiḥḥat al-taqsīm (sound division), which has been alluded to before. It left no category of the deterrents to acceptance that arise in hearts without bringing it. Do you not see that, after His saying «أفي قلوبهم مرض», He mentioned doubt (al-rība)? For the deterrent from responding to the judgement of Allah and His Messenger must be either concealing disbelief while displaying Islam — that is the sickness; or doubting, hesitating and wavering about Allah's judgement, whether it runs according to justice or otherwise — that is the doubt; or the deterrent is the fear of injustice, with which no hope of fairness is felt. So no category of deterrents remained but was mentioned. Then He, Glorified is He, sealed it with His saying «بل أولئك هم الظالمون», so it becomes a preparation (tarshīḥ) for the īghāl (closing intensification) that came at the end (fāṣila) of the verse: He established injustice as a description of them in replying to them, so that its affirmation in them would remain, and its existence in His judgement, Glorified is He [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense appears to be that injustice is affirmed of them and its opposite, justice, of His judgement]. From this arises al-iftinān (combining two genres), which is the speech combining the two arts of boasting and satire: for in describing them with injustice there is the description of His own Self with justice, and the description of His Prophet with justice as well. If you add to this that the speech has been cast in a mould of decorum and modesty, and that the bitter satire contains what does not suggest satire — and this is among the most cutting and most stinging of satire — then you have added to what preceded the device of nazāha (decency), a well-known rhetorical device which Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ expressed in his saying:
"The best satire is that which a virgin recites in her chamber without it being unseemly for one like her"; and Ibn Bassām in his saying in al-Dhakhīra: "Satire is divided into two kinds: a kind they call the satire of the nobles, which does not reach the point of being abuse or repulsive lampoon; and the second, the abuse which Jarīr and his class introduced." Thus there are combined in the verse good division (ḥusn al-taqsīm), īghāl, iftinān and nazāha.
Among the painful satire that contains no obscene word is the saying of Abū Tammām:
بني لهيعة ما بالي وبالكم ... وفي البلاد مناديح ومضطرب
لجاجة لي فيكم ليس يشبهها ... إلا لجاجتكم في أنكم عرب
(O Banū Lahīʿa, what is it with me and you, when in the lands there is ample room and space to roam? It is a stubbornness of mine about you, matched only by your stubbornness in [claiming] that you are Arabs.)

* Benefits:
Placing the khabar between the defective verbs and their nouns is permissible. Ibn Mālik said: «وفي جميعها توسط الخبر أجز» ("In all of them, permit the khabar's being placed in the middle"). Allah the Exalted said: «وكان حقا علينا نصر المؤمنين»: (حقا) is the fronted khabar of kāna and (نصر المؤمنين) its postponed noun. It is gathered from the words of al-Mughnī that putting the khabar in the nominative is weak, like the weakness of predicating a pronoun of what is lower than it in definiteness [Translator's note: so in the source], unless something prevents the fronting of the khabar, such as the khabar being restricted, as in «وما كان صلاتهم عند البيت إلا مكاء وتصدية», or the case-endings of both being hidden, as in «كان موسى فتاك». The placing in the middle may be obligatory, as in «كان في الدار ساكنها». So three categories result: a category that is permitted, a category that is prohibited and a category that is obligatory. They were silent about the fronting of their nouns [before the verbs] because it cannot be conceived: for whenever the noun is placed first, it becomes a mubtadaʾ and the abrogating verb (nāsikh) carries its pronoun, so it is not said that the noun was placed first.

dervis-irab:54-55.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ) A resumptive statement set out to address those commanded to obey on His part, Exalted is He. The clause (أطيعوا) is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); the Divine Name is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (أطيعوا الرسول) is conjoined to (أطيعوا الله). (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّما عَلَيْهِ ما حُمِّلَ وَعَلَيْكُمْ ما حُمِّلْتُمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (تولوا) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and it is an imperfect from which one of its two tāʾs has been dropped. (فإنما): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is omitted, i.e. if you turn away from obedience after you were commanded to it, then know that upon him (peace be upon him) is only what he was charged with, i.e. what he was commanded of conveying [the message]. (إنما) is the restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle; (عليه) is a fronted khabar (predicate) and (ما حمل) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (حمل) is the ṣila (relative clause); and (وعليكم ما حملتم) is conjoined to what preceded. (وَإِنْ تُطِيعُوهُ تَهْتَدُوا وَما عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (تطيعوه) is the protasis — a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its direct object; (تهتدوا) is the apodosis. The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; (ما) is negative; (على الرسول) is a fronted khabar; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (البلاغ) is a postponed mubtadaʾ and (المبين) an adjective. (وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ) A resumptive statement set out to establish the destiny of the believers who do righteous deeds and their being given power in the land. (وعد الله الذين) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; (منكم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to (آمنوا). The second object of (وعد) is omitted, its implied form being "succession" (al-istikhlāf), because His saying (ليستخلفنهم) indicates it. The lām is the answer to an implied oath, i.e. "I swear He will surely make them successors"; (في الأرض) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يستخلفنهم). You may treat (وعد) as (أقسم), so that it is answered with what an oath is answered with. (كَمَا اسْتَخْلَفَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ) The kāf is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a succession like the succession of those before them"; (الذين) is the object of (استخلف), and (من قبلهم) is attached to an omitted [element], the ṣila of (الذين). (وَلَيُمَكِّنَنَّ لَهُمْ دِينَهُمُ الَّذِي ارْتَضى لَهُمْ) (وليمكنن) is conjoined to (ليستخلفنهم); it is an imperfect indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its being attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis. (لهم) is attached to (يمكنن); (دينهم) is the direct object; (الذي) is an adjective; the clause (ارتضى) is the ṣila, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "which He approved"; and (لهم) is attached to (ارتضى). (وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ خَوْفِهِمْ أَمْناً) (وليبدلنهم) is conjoined to what preceded; the hāʾ is the first direct object; (من بعد خوفهم) is a ḥāl; and (أمنا) is the second direct object. (يَعْبُدُونَنِي لا يُشْرِكُونَ بِي شَيْئاً وَمَنْ كَفَرَ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ) The clause (يعبدونني) is resumptive according to the more likely view, so it has no grammatical position, as though it were the answer to an implied question, i.e. "What is their state?" and it was said: "They worship Me." Some parsers chose that it be a ḥāl of the object of (وعد), i.e. Allah promised them that in the state of their worship and sincerity, so its position is accusative; or a ḥāl of the object of (ليستخلفنهم). The clause (لا يشركون بي شيئا) is a badal (substitute) of it; you may make it a ḥāl of the agent of (يعبدونني), i.e. "they worship Me, affirming [My] oneness" — and this is good — and you may make it resumptive like the one before it. (شيئا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a direct object; its like has preceded often. (ومن كفر): the wāw is resumptive; (من) is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; (كفر) is a past verb, the protasis; (بعد ذلك) is attached to (كفر). (فأولئك هم الفاسقون): the clause is the apodosis, and the parsing of its parallel has preceded.

* Benefits:
History records that the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions remained in Mecca for ten years in fear, and when they emigrated they were in Medina, rising in the morning in arms and retiring in the evening in them, until a man said: "Will there not come upon us a day on which we are secure and lay down our arms?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "You will not remain but a little while until a man among you sits in a great assembly, sitting with his garment wrapped round his knees (muḥtabiyan), with no iron weapon on him." So Allah fulfilled His promise, gave them victory over the Arabian Peninsula, and they conquered the lands of the East and the West, tore apart the kingdom of the Chosroes, possessed their treasuries and took control of the world. Then came forth those who were contrary to their conduct, and they were ungrateful for those blessings and acted wickedly. That is his saying ﷺ: "The caliphate after me is thirty years; then Allah gives kingship to whom He wills, and it becomes kingship; then it becomes bizzīzā — cutting of the roads, shedding of blood and taking of wealth without right." As for the meaning of bizzīzā, he said in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: bazzahu yabuzzuhu bazzan: he robbed him; and the noun is al-bizzīzā, like al-khiṣṣīṣā.

dervis-irab:30-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَغْضُضْنَ): al-ghaḍḍ is closing the eyelids so that seeing is prevented. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Ghaḍḍa al-rajulu ṣawtahu wa-ṭarfahu, and min ṣawtihi and min ṭarfihi, ghaḍḍan, of the pattern of qatala: he lowered [his voice or gaze]. From this one says ghaḍḍa min fulān, ghaḍḍan and ghaḍāḍatan, when he disparaged him." In the first, one of the two identical letters has been assimilated (udghima) into the second, unlike the second, because the second in يغضضن is vowelled, so the first was assimilated into it, while in what follows it is quiescent, so assimilation of the first into it was not possible. Jarīr said:
فغض الطرف إنك من نمير ... فلا كعبا بلغت ولا كلابا
(So lower your gaze, for you are of Numayr; you have reached neither Kaʿb nor Kilāb.)
[Translator's note: the reasoning on assimilation is translated as written; in fact the doubled letter is assimilated in يغضوا, where the second ḍād is vowelled, and left unassimilated in يغضضن, where it is quiescent before the nūn of the feminine plural.]
(زِينَتَهُنَّ): adornment (al-zīna) is that with which a woman adorns herself: jewellery, kohl or dye (khiḍāb). What is outward of it — such as the ring, the fatakha (with vowelled tāʾ), which is a ring of silver without a stone (if it has a stone it is a khātam), kohl and dye — there is no harm in showing to strangers. What is hidden of it — such as the bracelet, the anklet, the armlet, the necklace, the iklīl (which, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, resembles a headband adorned with jewels; the crown is also called iklīl), the sash (wishāḥ) and the earring — she does not show except to those mentioned.
(بِخُمُرِهِنَّ): al-khumur, with ḍamma on the khāʾ and the mīm, is the plural of khimār, with kasra on the khāʾ, which is what a woman covers her head with, and a covering in general. It is pluralised as akhmira, khumr (with ḍamma on the khāʾ and sukūn on the mīm) and khumur (with two ḍammas).
