(Truly, an eye that did not pour its flowing tears for you on the day of Wāsiṭ is dry indeed — on the evening when the wailing women stood up, and collars and cheeks were torn by the hands of a mourning gathering. If your courtyard is now deserted, many a time delegations stayed in it after delegations.)
Wāsiṭ is the site of the battle in which al-Manṣūr killed Ibn Hubayra. Al-maʾtam is the place of staying; it was used metaphorically for a gathering of grieving women, and its plural is maʾātim. He says: every eye that did not weep for you that day is extremely dry. (عشية) is a badal (substitute) of (يوم). The jayb of a shirt is the opening for the head, i.e. the collars and cheeks were torn by the women's hands. Then he turned to direct address. His saying «فإن تمس مهجور الفناء» is a metonymy (kināya) for death. «فربما», i.e. often, crowds of people stayed in the courtyard of your house after crowds, seeking your gifts; so if your courtyard is deserted now, there is no grief, for often people gathered in it and were granted good.

dervis-irab:39-40.t:
* Vocabulary:
(كَسَرابٍ): al-sarāb (mirage) is what is seen at midday from the intensity of the heat, as though it were water in which houses, trees and other things are reflected. It is proverbial for lying and deception; one says: "He is more deceptive than a mirage." It is called sarāb because it yatasarrab, i.e. flows like water; one says sariba al-faḥl, i.e. [the stallion] went off and travelled. It is also called al-āl. It occurs only in the open desert and in heat, and the thirsty one is deceived by it.
(بِقِيعَةٍ): al-qīʿa means al-qāʿ, or is a plural of qāʿ, which is flat, level ground. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "Al-qāʿ is level ground; the plural is aqwāʿ and qīʿān, the wāw having become yāʾ because of the kasra before it. Al-qīʿa is like al-qāʿ, and it too is from the wāw-root; some say it is a plural." Al-Harawī said: "Al-qīʿa is the plural of al-qāʿ, like jīra and jār." In al-Asās: "It is like a mirage in a qīʿa and in a qāʿ; they alighted at a mirage of plains (qīʿān); they have a spacious qāʿa, which is the open courtyard of the house. The people of Mecca call the lower part of the house al-qāʿa, and they say: so-and-so sat in the ʿaliyya [upper room] and put his goods in the qāʿa." And [the poet] said:
سائل مجاور جرم هل جنيت لهم ... حربا تفرّق بين الجيرة الخلط
وهل تركت نساء الحي ضاحية ... في قاعة الدار يستوقدن بالغبط
(Ask the neighbours of Jarm whether I brought upon them a war that separated the mingled neighbours, and whether I left the women of the clan exposed in the courtyard of the house, kindling fires with the camel-litters' frames.)
[Translator's note: the source prints «العسية», evidently for «العِلِّيَّة» (the upper room); translated accordingly.]
In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj there is what makes it understood that al-qāʿ is easy, low-lying land from which the mountains and hills have parted; it is pluralised as aqwāʿ, aqwuʿ, qīʿ, qīʿān and qīʿa.
(لُجِّيٍّ): al-lujjiyy is deep, abundant in water, a nisba to al-lujj, which is the main body of the sea — so al-Zamakhsharī said. Others said it is a nisba to al-lujja, with tāʾ, which is also its main body.

* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَعْمالُهُمْ كَسَرابٍ بِقِيعَةٍ يَحْسَبُهُ الظَّمْآنُ ماءً حَتَّى إِذا جاءَهُ لَمْ يَجِدْهُ شَيْئاً): resumptive (mustaʾnaf) speech, brought to set out the state of the deeds of one who does not hold faith nor follow the truth, after He set out the state of the believers by striking a parable for them, namely «مثل نوره كمشكاة». الذين is the first mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; أعمالهم is a second mubtadaʾ; كسراب is the khabar (predicate) of the second; the second mubtadaʾ with its khabar is the khabar of the first. The clause يحسبه الظمآن is a naʿt (adjective) of سراب; ماء is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يحسبه; حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause جاءه is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it; the clause لم يجده has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; شيئا stands in the place of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. he did not find it with any finding. It is also said that شيئا here means what he had estimated and supposed, so it is a second direct object of يجده. More discussion of it will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَوَجَدَ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ فَوَفَّاهُ حِسابَهُ وَاللَّهُ سَرِيعُ الْحِسابِ): the wāw is a conjunction; وجد is a past verb with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent); the Name of Majesty is the direct object; عنده is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second direct object of وجد, i.e. being at the mirage, or at the deed. فوفاه: the fāʾ is a conjunction; وفاه is a verb, a latent agent and the first direct object; حسابه is the second direct object, i.e. He requited him for it in this world [sic]. الله is a mubtadaʾ and سريع الحساب the khabar.
[Translator's note: «في الدنيا» ("in this world") is as printed in the source; the context of the verse concerns the Hereafter.]
(أَوْ كَظُلُماتٍ فِي بَحْرٍ لُجِّيٍّ يَغْشاهُ مَوْجٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ مَوْجٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ سَحابٌ): أو is a conjunction; it is said to be for division or for choice, i.e. the unbeliever's deeds are of two kinds: a kind like the mirage, namely the good deed, and a kind like the darknesses, namely the evil deed; or that the unbeliever's deed is void and of no benefit, like the mirage, and, because it is devoid of the light of truth, like piled-up darknesses and pitch-black glooms. Al-Zajjāj said: "Allah, Glorified is He, made known that the deeds of the unbelievers, just as they resemble the mirage described with those qualities, also resemble the darknesses; and that if they are likened to what is found, their likeness is that of the mirage, and if they are likened to what is seen, they are like these darknesses that He described." He also said: "If you wish, liken them to the mirage, and if you wish, liken them to these darknesses; so أو is for permission (ibāḥa)." The preposition and its genitive noun are coordinated with كسراب, with an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "or like one in darknesses"; this muḍāf is indicated by His words «إذا أخرج يده لم يكد يراها»; or with two omitted muḍāfs, their implied form being "like the deeds of one in darknesses". في بحر is a naʿt of ظلمات; لجي is a naʿt of بحر; the clause يغشاه موج is a second naʿt of بحر; موج is the agent; من فوقه is a fronted khabar and موج a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being a naʿt of the first موج; the clause من فوقه سحاب is a naʿt of the second موج.
(ظُلُماتٌ بَعْضُها فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ إِذا أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَراها): ظلمات is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. these are darknesses, and the clause is an explanation of what precedes it, so it has no grammatical position. بعضها is a mubtadaʾ; فوق بعض: the adverb is attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is a naʿt of ظلمات. إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition, attached to the apodosis; the clause أخرج is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it; the agent of أخرج is the pronoun of the one who is in the sea, floundering in it; يده is the direct object. لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive government; يكد is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم; its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; the clause يراها is the khabar of يكد; the clause لم يكد يراها has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
(وَمَنْ لَمْ يَجْعَلِ اللَّهُ لَهُ نُوراً فَما لَهُ مِنْ نُورٍ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive-governing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive government; يجعل is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); الله is the agent; له is the second direct object and نورا the first direct object of يجعل; the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it is a nominal clause; ما is negative; له is a fronted khabar; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; نور is genitive in form and nominative in position as mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains varieties of rhetoric, which we set out below:
1- The explicit simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal): He has brought what the senses do not perceive out into what the senses perceive. Had it been said "the onlooker thinks it water", it would have been eloquent, but the wording of the Qur'an is more eloquent, because the thirsty one is more eager for it and his heart more attached to it. Likening the deeds of the unbelievers to a mirage is among the finest and most eloquent of similes — how much more so when it also contains beauty of composition, sweetness of words, soundness of signification and truth of representation.
2- The representative simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī): His words «ووجد الله عنده» are a representative simile, i.e. he found His punishment and the guards of His torment. The point of comparison is that the unbeliever performs works of piety and believes that he has a reward with Allah the Exalted, but it is not so; when he arrives at the plains of the Resurrection he does not find the reward he supposed, but finds immense punishment and painful torment, so his regret becomes great and his grief reaches its limit. His state is likened to the state of the thirsty man whose need for water has become intense: when he sees the mirage in the open land his heart clings to it, and when he comes to it he finds it to be nothing. Such is the state of the unbeliever: he reckons that his deed will benefit him, and when he needs his deed he finds it has availed him nothing.
3- Conjunction to something omitted: in His words, Exalted is He, «وَوَجَدَ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ», there is conjunction to something implied. The clause is not conjoined to «لم يجده شيئا» but to what is understood from it by way of representation: the unbelievers' finding neither substance nor trace of their mentioned deeds. It is as though it were said: until, when the unbelievers come on the Day of Resurrection to their deeds which in this world they reckoned would benefit them in the Hereafter, they find them to be nothing, and they find Allah's judgement and decree lying in wait for them.
4- Hyperbole in the simile: this is in His words «إذا أخرج يده لم يكد يراها». People have differed over the interpretation of this speech, and there is near-consensus that the meaning is that he does not see his hand. On this there are three views regarding the implied construction:
One is that the implied form is "he did not see it, nor almost [see it]"; this is unclear, because it is a negation of seeing and then an affirmation of it. A second view is that كاد is redundant, and there is no room for that in the Qur'an. So the [correct] view, then, is that he did not come near to seeing it, let alone see it. Similar is the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
إذا غيّر النأي المحبين لم يكد ... رسيس الهوى من حب مية يبرح
(When distance changes lovers, the lingering trace of passion from the love of Mayya hardly departs.)
i.e. it does not come near to departing. Al-naʾy: distance. One says rassa and arassa when something clings; al-rasīs is the remnant of an illness; yabraḥ: it goes away. It is related that when Dhū al-Rumma came to Kufa, Ibn Shubruma objected to him about this, on the grounds that it indicates the passing of the trace of passion, so he changed it to «لم أجد» (I did not find). Ibn ʿUtba said: I told my father about that, and he said: Ibn Shubruma was wrong, and Dhū al-Rumma was wrong to change it; it is just like His words, Exalted is He, «لم يكد يراها». After the verse comes:
فلا القرب يدنو من هواها ملالة ... ولا حبها إن تنزح الدار ينزح
(Nearness does not bring weariness close to my love for her, nor does her love depart if the dwelling departs far away.)
[Translator's note: the source says "three views" but only the views it lists are translated; it also prints «اتبات» for «إثبات» (affirmation).]

dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الزَّانِيَةُ): from the root of al-zinā and al-zināʾ, with the long and the short [final vowel]. Al-Farazdaq said:
أبا خالد من يزن يعلم زناؤه ... ومن يشرب الخرطوم يصبح مسكّرا
(Abū Khālid, whoever commits adultery, his adultery becomes known, and whoever drinks the choicest wine wakes up drunk.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: the short form is from zanā and the long form from zānā; one says zānāhā, muzānātan and zināʾan; so-and-so (a woman) went out tuzānī and tubāghī (to commit fornication and harlotry); he committed adultery with her (zanā bihā); he gathered the zunāt and the zawānī; zannāhu, tazniyatan: he attributed adultery to him; and he is a child of zinya (illegitimate), with fatḥa or kasra on the zāy.
(رَأْفَةٌ): in al-Mukhtār: «Raʾfa is the most intense mercy. Raʾufa, with ḍamma, raʾāfatan; raʾafa bihi, yarʾafu, like qaṭaʿa, yaqṭaʿu; and raʾifa bihi, on the pattern of ṭariba; all of it is from the speech of the Arabs; so he is raʾūf, on the pattern faʿūl.»

* I'rab:
(سُورَةٌ أَنْزَلْناها وَفَرَضْناها وَأَنْزَلْنا فِيها آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ) (سورة) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a sūra"; or a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, i.e. "among what We have revealed to you is a sūra". Beginning with an indefinite noun is permissible because it is described by the clause (أنزلناها). (فرضناها) is conjoined to (أنزلناها), and (أنزلنا) is also conjoined; (فيها) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزلنا); (آيات) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (بينات) an adjective of (آيات). Laʿalla and its noun, and the clause (تذكرون) its khabar; the clause (لعلكم تذكرون) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(الزَّانِيَةُ وَالزَّانِي فَاجْلِدُوا كُلَّ واحِدٍ مِنْهُما مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ) A resumptive clause, introduced to begin detailing the clear verses that were mentioned. On the nominative of (الزانية) and (الزاني) there are two views. The first is the school of Sībawayh: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "among what is recited to you is the ruling on the adulteress…". The second is the school of al-Akhfash and others: that it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is the imperative clause, the fāʾ entering because of the resemblance of the mubtadaʾ to a condition. This question was discussed exhaustively at His saying «والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما», so refresh your memory of it; more of this discussion will come in the Benefits section.
He put (الزانية) before (الزاني) only because she is the origin of the act, since the inducement to it [comes] more abundantly from her, and were it not for her enabling him it would not occur. The matter is reversed in the verse on the penalty for theft, where He put the male thief before the female thief, because adultery is generated by the desire for intercourse, which is stronger and greater in woman, whereas theft is generated by boldness, strength and daring, which are stronger and greater in man.
(فاجلدوا): the fāʾ is a link, because the alif-lām [article] is in the sense of (الذي), and the relative noun has a scent of the condition in it, i.e. "she who committed adultery and he who committed adultery, flog them both", as you say "whoever commits adultery, flog him". (اجلدوا) is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); (كل واحد) is a mafʿūl bihi; (منهما) is an adjective of (واحد); (مائة جلدة) is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because the mafʿūl muṭlaq may be substituted by its number, i.e. [a hundred] blows. One says jaladahu: he struck his skin (jild). (وَلا تَأْخُذْكُمْ بِهِما رَأْفَةٌ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (تأخذكم) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you" [Translator's note: so in the source; the fāʿil is (رأفة), as the source itself says next]; (بهما) is attached to (تأخذكم); (رأفة) is the fāʿil; and (في دين الله) is also attached to (تأخذكم). (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ) (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a defective past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause (تؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر) is the khabar of (كنتم). The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then let no pity for them seize you in the religion of Allah and His ruling". What is intended by the condition is to stir up and rouse indignation against adulterers and anger for the sake of Allah and His religion.
More discussion of this verse will come in the Rhetoric section. (وَلْيَشْهَدْ عَذابَهُما طائِفَةٌ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ)
The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; (يشهد) is an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām; (عذابهما) is a fronted mafʿūl bihi and (طائفة) a postponed fāʿil; (من المؤمنين) is an adjective of (طائفة). The discussion of what is meant by it will come.
(الزَّانِي لا يَنْكِحُ إِلَّا زانِيَةً أَوْ مُشْرِكَةً) A resumptive clause, introduced to show that the vile, sinful man who has made adultery his habit and constant practice does not desire to marry righteous women of chastity and virtue; and likewise the vile, sinful woman refuses anything but to plunge into the unwholesome pit of filth. (الزاني) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا ينكح) the khabar; (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and the secret of the restriction will come in the Rhetoric section. (زانية) is a mafʿūl bihi; (أو) is a conjunction and (مشركة) is conjoined to (زانية). (وَالزَّانِيَةُ لا يَنْكِحُها إِلَّا زانٍ أَوْ مُشْرِكٌ) A clause conjoined to the previous one and like it in i'rab. (زان) is the fāʿil; its yāʾ has been omitted because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ), whose yāʾ is omitted with tanwīn in the nominative and genitive and retained in the accusative. (وَحُرِّمَ ذلِكَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, introduced to state the ruling on those who imitate the sinful and expose themselves to evil talk and slander. The discussion of the secret of the prohibition will come in the Benefits section.
(وَالَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ الْمُحْصَناتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَداءَ) The wāw is resumptive, introduced to state another kind of the penalties relating to adultery. (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ which will have three khabars; the clause (يرمون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (المحصنات) is a mafʿūl bihi; (ثم لم يأتوا) is conjoined to (يرمون); (بأربعة) is attached to (يأتوا); (شهداء) is muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the fatḥa because it is a diptote, owing to the feminine alif in it. (فَاجْلِدُوهُمْ ثَمانِينَ جَلْدَةً وَلا تَقْبَلُوا لَهُمْ شَهادَةً أَبَداً وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ) The fāʾ links the answer of the relative noun, which contains the sense of a condition; (اجلدوهم) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause (فاجلدوهم) is the first khabar of (الذين); (ثمانين) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq and (جلدة) a tamyīz (specification). (ولا تقبلوا) is conjoined to (فاجلدوهم), and it stands as the second khabar of (الذين); (لهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of (شهادة); (أبدا) is an adverb attached to (تقبلوا). In (وأولئك) the wāw is a conjunction; (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (هم) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), or a second [mubtadaʾ] [Translator's note: the source has «خبر ثان» (a second khabar), apparently for «مبتدأ ثان»]; (الفاسقون) is the khabar of (أولئك) or the khabar of (هم); and the clause stands as the third khabar of (الذين). (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تابُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ وَأَصْلَحُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (إلا) is a particle of exception and (الذين) is excepted from (الفاسقين). There is disagreement over this exception. It was said that it is connected (muttaṣil), because what is excepted from is in reality (الذين يرمون), and those who repent are among them, but they are taken out of the ruling, and this is the nature of the connected [exception]. It was also said that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), because it was not intended to take him out of the preceding ruling, but rather to affirm another matter for him, namely that one who repents does not remain sinful (fāsiq); and because he is not included in the beginning of the speech, since he is not sinful. The clause (تابوا) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (من بعد ذلك) is attached to (تابوا); (أصلحوا) is conjoined to (تابوا). In (فإن) the fāʾ gives the reason for what precedes; inna and its noun; (غفور) is its first khabar and (رحيم) its second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- Concision by omission (al-ījāz bil-ḥadhf):
In His saying «سُورَةٌ أَنْزَلْناها» there is concision by omission. As ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī sees it, it is a topic subtle in its path, fine in its approach, wondrous in its nature, resembling magic; for through it you see that leaving something unmentioned is more eloquent than mentioning it, and silence about conveying [information] conveys more, and you find yourself most articulate when you do not speak and most complete in expression when you do not express. But ʿAbd al-Qāhir did not hit the heart of the truth when he went on to say: «There is no noun omitted in a situation in which it ought to be omitted but that its omission is better than its mention.» The reason he did not hit it is that what he mentioned does not hold for every mubtadaʾ; it is good only for a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is a description implying praise or blame, which admits of intensification, such that this intensification conveys a meaning about the one described. Among mubtadaʾs there are those otherwise: in our saying "Zayd is standing" we find in describing Zayd as standing no particularity by which Zayd is distinguished from others, for anyone may be described as standing when the opposite of sitting is meant; it does not admit intensification; it is neither among the attributes of praise nor among those of blame; nor is it something by which the one described reaches [the point] that he alone deserves to be described by it. If the Qāḍī [Translator's note: so in the source; ʿAbd al-Qāhir is meant], may Allah have mercy on him, meant a specific mubtadaʾ, then it is possible; but if he spoke absolutely, the matter is problematic, and the reason for its omission that he mentioned is not known.
Then ʿAbd al-Qāhir presents examples from fine poetry of verses in which the mubtadaʾ is omitted, as in the poet's saying:
سأشكر عمرا إن تراخت منيتي ... أيادي لم تمنن وإن هي جلّت
(I shall thank ʿAmr, if my death is delayed, for favours not reproached, however great they were.)
فتى غير محجوب الغنى عن صديقه ... ولا مظهر الشكوى إذا النعل زلت
(A young man whose wealth is not withheld from his friend, nor does he show complaint when the sandal slips.)
The original is: "He is a young man".
2- Prohibition and condition for stirring up:
What is intended by the prohibition in His saying «ولا تأخذكم» and the condition in His saying «إن كنتم تؤمنون…» is stirring up, rousing anger and inflaming zeal for the religion of Allah; and the believers who are keen to bear this radiant mark must be firm in their religion and not be seized by leniency or softness in carrying out what Allah commanded them in fully executing His penalties (ḥudūd). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the example with himself and his daughter, saying: «If Fāṭima the daughter of Muhammad were to steal, I would cut off her hand.»
3- Restriction (ḥaṣr) by (إلا):
The apparent wording suggests that the adulterer does not marry the chaste believing woman and that the adulteress is not married by the God-fearing believer. Since that is not evidently correct, the statement must be taken as referring to the general and the predominant, as [when one says] "none does good but the God-fearing man", while one who is not God-fearing may do good.
4- He used rami (throwing) metaphorically for reviling with the indecency of adultery, because it is an offence by speech, as al-Nābigha said:
وجرح اللسان كجرح اليد
(And the wound of the tongue is like the wound of the hand.)
Reviling with this indecency is called qadhf (throwing). What is meant by (المحصنات) is women; He singled them out for mention because slandering them is more heinous and the disgrace in them greater. Men are joined to women in this ruling without disagreement among the scholars of this community.

* Benefits:
1- His saying «الزَّانِيَةُ وَالزَّانِي فَاجْلِدُوا», the verse: al-Khalīl and Sībawayh turned to the i'rab we have transmitted for two reasons, one verbal and one semantic. The verbal one is that the speech is a command, which suggests that the accusative is to be preferred; yet the nominative is the reading of the generality. Had the command been made a khabar and the mubtadaʾ built upon it, it would be contrary to what is preferred among the eloquent; so he resorted to assuming the khabar, so that the mubtadaʾ would not be built upon the command, and thereby escaped contradicting the preference. Sībawayh illustrated them in his Book with His saying «مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ فِيها أَنْهارٌ», the verse. The point of the illustration is that He began the speech with His saying «مثل الجنة», and His saying «فيها أنهار» cannot properly be its khabar, so it is necessary to assume its khabar omitted, its original being "among what We relate to you is the likeness of the Garden"; then, since this was a summary mention of the likeness, He detailed the summary with His saying «فيها أنهار» to its end. So likewise here, as though He said:
"Among what has been prescribed for you is the matter of the adulteress and the adulterer", then He detailed this summary with the rulings on flogging that He mentioned. This is the explanation of what required, for Sībawayh, the choice of omission from the standpoint of verbal craft. As for the standpoint of meaning, it is that the meaning is more complete and perfect with the khabar omitted, because He will have mentioned the ruling on the adulteress and the adulterer in summary when He said (الزانية والزاني), meaning "among what has been prescribed for you is the ruling on the adulteress and the adulterer"; then, when the listener longed for the detail of this summary, He mentioned their ruling in detail, which makes a deeper impression on the soul than mentioning it at the first instance.
2- His saying «وَلْيَشْهَدْ عَذابَهُما طائِفَةٌ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ»: al-ṭāʾifa is a group that can form a circle, its minimum being three or four. It is an adjective that has come to be used predominantly [as a noun], as though it were the group surrounding a thing. From Ibn ʿAbbās in its explanation: it is from four to forty men of those who believe in Allah; from al-Ḥasan: ten; from Qatāda: three or more; from ʿIkrima: two men or more; from Mujāhid: its minimum is one man or more; and it was said: two men. The view of Ibn ʿAbbās is preferred, because four is the group by which the penalty is established; the details are in the books of jurisprudence.
3- The four categories of adulterers:
a- The adulterer desires none but an adulteress.
b- The adulteress desires none but an adulterer.
c- The chaste man desires none but a chaste woman.
d- The chaste woman desires none but a chaste man.
These four categories differ in meaning and exhaust the division. So we say: the verse abridged two categories out of these four and confined itself to two that are more fitting [to mention] than the two passed over in silence, so it came concise and comprehensive. The first [statement] is explicit about the first category and conveys the third by implication; the second [statement] is explicit about the second category and conveys the fourth. The third and fourth categories entail each other, in that what requires the chaste man's desire to be confined to the chaste woman is their sharing in the attribute, and that very thing requires her desire to be confined to him. Then the expression is confined to the description of adulterers and of the chaste in a way no less than the mention of adulterers, positively and negatively [Translator's note: this sentence is obscure in the source]; for the meaning of the first is: the adulteress is not married by a chaste man, and the meaning of the second: the chaste woman is not married by an adulterer. The secret in that is that the discussion is about their rulings, so He mentioned the chaste [only] to negate their defects, so that the speech would not depart from its intended purpose. Then He made it clear [Translator's note: so in the source] in attributing marriage in these two categories to the males rather than the females, unlike His saying (الزانية والزاني), where He gave each of them an independent [mention] and put the adulteress before the adulterer, as preceded. The reason for this is that the first discussion is about the ruling on adultery, in which the woman is the origin, because of the flirting and enticement that appear from her; while the second discussion is about the marriage of adulterers when it takes place validly, and in marriage the origin is the males, who are the ones who begin the proposal; so it was attributed only to them for this reason. Even so, the purpose of the verse is to make the chaste, male and female, averse to marrying adulterers, male and female, to deter them from indecency; for that reason adultery and polytheism were coupled.

dervis-irab:41-44.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الطَّيْرُ): Abū ʿUbayda and Quṭrub said: al-ṭayr applies to the singular and the plural. Ibn al-Anbārī said: al-ṭayr is a collective, and treating it as feminine is more frequent than as masculine. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Al-ṭāʾir is on the form of the active participle of ṭāra, yaṭīru, ṭayarānan; flying is for it in the air like the walking of animals on the ground. It is made transitive by the hamza and by doubling, so one says ṭayyartuhu and aṭartuhu. The plural of al-ṭāʾir is ṭayr, like ṣāḥib and ṣaḥb, rākib and rakb; and the plural of al-ṭayr is ṭuyūr and aṭyār."
(صَافَّاتٍ): spreading their wings in the air.
(يُزْجِي): He drives. In al-Mukhtār: "Zajjā al-shayʾa, tazjiyatan: he pushed it gently; tazajjā bi-kadhā: he made do with it; azjā al-ibil: he drove the camels; al-muzjā is a small thing, and biḍāʿa muzjāt is scanty merchandise; the wind yuzjī the clouds, and the cow tuzjī her calf, i.e. drives it." In al-Qāmūs and its commentary: "Zajā, yazjū, zajwan; zajjā, tazjiyatan; azjā, izjāʾan; and izdajāhu: he drove it and pushed it gently. One says: how do you yuzjī your days?, i.e. how do you push them along. Zajjā fulān ḥājatī: he made obtaining my need easy. Azjā al-amr: he postponed the matter. Azjā al-dirham: he made the dirham pass current." From this is the saying of al-Nābigha:
إني أتيتك من أهلي ومن وطني ... أزجي حشاشة نفس ما بها رمق
(I have come to you from my family and my homeland, driving along the last breath of a soul in which there is no life left.)
(رُكاماً): al-rukām, with ḍamma on the rāʾ, is that which is heaped up, part of it on top of another. In al-Mukhtār: "Rakama al-shayʾa when he gathered it and threw part of it on another, of the pattern of naṣara; irtakama al-shayʾ and tarākama: it gathered together; al-rukām is heaped sand, and clouds and the like."
(الْوَدْقَ): rain. It is said to be specific to light rain, and it is said to be rain whether light or heavy. It is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); one says wadaqa al-saḥāb, yadiqu, of the pattern of waʿada.
(سَنا): in al-Mukhtār: "Al-sanā, with short final alif, is the gleam of lightning; al-sanā is also a plant used as medicine; al-sanāʾ, with long final alif, is from loftiness, and a lofty thing. Asnāhu: he raised it. Sannāhu, tasniyatan: he opened it and made it easy."

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): resumptive (mustaʾnaf) speech, brought to establish this truth. The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive government; تر is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you". أنّ and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of تر, because the seeing here is mental (qalbiyya), since the glorification of those who glorify is not something visual sight attaches to; i.e. you have known with a knowledge resembling eyewitness in certainty. The clause يسبح is the khabar (predicate) [of أنّ]; له is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يسبح; من is the agent of يسبح; في السموات والأرض is the ṣila (relative clause) of من.
(وَالطَّيْرُ صَافَّاتٍ كُلٌّ قَدْ عَلِمَ صَلاتَهُ وَتَسْبِيحَهُ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِما يَفْعَلُونَ): the wāw is for conjunction; الطير is conjoined to من; صافات is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the object of صافات is omitted, i.e. spreading their wings. كل is a mubtadaʾ (subject); beginning with it is permissible because of the sense of generality in it; the clause قد علم is the khabar of كل. The agent of علم refers to كل or to Allah. Abū al-Baqāʾ says that its referring to «كل» is preferable, "because the reading has كل in the nominative as mubtadaʾ, so the agent pronoun refers back to it. If it contained a pronoun of the name of Allah, it would be preferable to put كل in the accusative, because the verb after it has governed in the accusative something connected with it (min sababihā); it would become like your saying زيدا ضرب عمر وغلامه (Zayd — ʿAmr struck his servant), where you put Zayd in the accusative by a verb indicated by what follows it, and that is stronger than the nominative, though the other is permissible." صلاته is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وتسبيحه is conjoined to صلاته; الله is a mubtadaʾ and عليم the khabar; بما is attached to عليم; the clause يفعلون is the ṣila of ما.
(وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ الْمَصِيرُ): the wāw is resumptive; لله is a fronted khabar and ملك السموات والأرض a postponed mubtadaʾ; إلى الله is a fronted khabar and المصير a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُزْجِي سَحاباً ثُمَّ يُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُ ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ رُكاماً): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation; أنّ and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of تر; the i'rab of its counterpart has preceded. ثم is a conjunction; يؤلف is conjoined to يزجي; بينه is an adverb attached to يؤلف. بين has entered upon a singular, whereas it only enters upon a dual or more, because either the genus is meant by السحاب, so the pronoun refers back according to its [plural] status, or it is meant to be with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. between its pieces, for each piece is a cloud (saḥāba). ثم is a conjunction; يجعله is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and the first direct object; ركاما is the second direct object.
(فَتَرَى الْوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلالِهِ وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ مِنْ جِبالٍ فِيها مِنْ بَرَدٍ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; ترى الودق is an imperfect verb, a latent agent whose implied form is "you", and a direct object; the clause يخرج is a ḥāl, because the seeing here is visual; من خلاله is attached to يخرج, i.e. from its rifts and outlets, plural of khalal, like jabal and jibāl. ينزل من السماء من جبال فيها من برد: its i'rab has preceded, and we repeat it here for reinforcement. The first من is of beginning (ibtidāʾiyya), attached to ينزل; likewise the second, which is a badal (substitute) with repetition of the governing word; فيها is a naʿt (adjective) of جبال; من برد is partitive, and it with its genitive noun is in the position of the object of sending down. It is also said to be explicative (li-l-bayān), so that it would be a ḥāl, and من جبال would be in the position of the object of sending down. Someone summarised the i'rab of the verse, saying: the upshot is that من in من السماء is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya) without disagreement; and in من in من جبال فيها there are three views. First: it is for the beginning of the extent, so it with its genitive noun is a badal of the first, with repetition of the preposition, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl).
Second: it is partitive, so on this it with its genitive noun is in the position of the accusative as the object of sending down, as though He said "and He sends down some mountains".
Third: it is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. He sends down mountains from the sky.
As for من in من برد, there are four views:
the three preceding ones, and the fourth that it is to explain the genus (li-bayān al-jins), so the implied form on this view is: "and He sends down from the sky some mountains which are hail".
Al-Zajjāj said: "The meaning of the verse is: and He sends down from the sky, from mountains of hail in it — as you say: 'This is a ring in my hand of iron', i.e. an iron ring in my hand, because if you say 'this is a ring of iron' or 'an iron ring', the meaning is the same." On this, من برد is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of جبال, just as من حديد is a naʿt of خاتم, and the object of ينزل is من جبال; and from the mountains being hail it follows that what is sent down is hail.
Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned that the implied form is "something from mountains", the qualified noun having been omitted and the qualifier sufficing.
(فَيُصِيبُ بِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَصْرِفُهُ عَنْ مَنْ يَشاءُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; يصيب is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun referring to Allah; به is attached to يصيب; من is the direct object; the clause يشاء is the ṣila of the relative; ويصرفه عمن يشاء is conjoined to the preceding clause and is parallel to it.
(يَكادُ سَنا بَرْقِهِ يَذْهَبُ بِالْأَبْصارِ) (يُقَلِّبُ اللَّهُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِأُولِي الْأَبْصارِ): the clause is a naʿt of برد [sic]. يكاد is an imperfect verb, one of the verbs of approximation; سنا برقه is its noun and the clause يذهب بالأبصار its khabar. The clause يقلب is an explanation of what precedes it, so it has no grammatical position; الله is the agent of يقلب; الليل is the direct object and النهار conjoined to الليل. إنّ is a particle resembling the verb; في ذلك is its fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); عبرة is its postponed noun; لأولي الأبصار is a naʿt of عبرة; الأبصار here means insights (al-baṣāʾir).
[Translator's note: the source says the clause «يكاد سنا برقه» qualifies «برد», though the pronoun in «برقه» refers to the clouds; translated as written.]

* Rhetoric:
1- The device of the "title" (fann al-ʿunwān):
In His words «ألم تر أن الله يزجي سحابا» — the verse — there is a device which only a few of the scholars of rhetoric have treated on its own, namely the device of the title. They defined it as the speaker taking up an aim of his — description, boasting, praise, reproach, satire or other genres — and then, to complete and reinforce it, bringing examples in words that serve as titles of earlier reports and past stories. Of it there is a very great kind, namely what serves as a title for sciences: that words are mentioned in speech which are keys to sciences and entrances to them. The verse we are dealing with contains the title of the science known as the upper phenomena (al-āthār al-ʿulwiyya, meteorology), mathematical geography and astronomy. Among its examples in poetry is the ode of Abū Firās al-Ḥamdānī:
خليلي ما أعددتما لمتيم ... أسير لدى الأعداء جافي المراقد
فريد عن الأحباب لكن دموعه ... مثان على الخدين غير فرائد
جمعت سيوف الهند من كل وجهة ... وأعددت للأعداء كل مجالد
إذا كان غير الله للمرء عدة ... أتته الرزايا من وجوه الفوائد
فقد جرت الحنفاء حتف جذيمة ... وكان يراها عدة للشدائد
وجرت منايا مالك بن نويرة ... حليلته الحسناء يا أم خالد
وأردى ذؤابا في بيوت عتيبة ... بنوه وأهلوه بشدو القصائد
(My two friends, what have you prepared for an enthralled lover, a captive among enemies, kept from his beds; parted from loved ones, yet his tears run in pairs down his cheeks, not singly? I gathered Indian swords from every direction and prepared every fighter against the enemies. When other than Allah is a man's provision, calamities come to him from the very sources of benefit. Al-Ḥanfāʾ [the mare] brought on the death of Jadhīma, though he counted her a provision for hardships; and the death of Mālik ibn Nuwayra was brought on by his beautiful wife, O Umm Khālid; and Dhuʾāb was brought to ruin in the houses of ʿUtayba by his sons and kin through the chanting of odes.)
[Translator's note: the fourth and fifth verses are run together in the source's line division; they are separated here without changing any word.]
These stories to which Abū Firās digressed, to complete his purpose and support his view, are famous and well known, and one can refer to them in their proper sources with ease.
Al-Farazdaq said to Jarīr:
فهل أنت إن ماتت أتانك راكب ... إلى آل بسطام بن قيس فخاطب
وإني لأخشى إن خطيت إليهم ... عليك الذي لاقى يسار الكواعب
(If your she-ass dies, will you ride to the family of Bisṭām ibn Qays and ask for a bride? I fear for you, if you seek a bride among them, what Yasār of the maidens met with.)
[Translator's note: «خطيت» is printed thus in the source, evidently for «خطبت» (you sought in marriage).]
Of the story of Yasār: he was a black slave who herded camels for his masters, and with him was a slave who herded with him. Yasār's master had a daughter. One day she passed by his camels while they were grazing in a grassy meadow, and Yasār brought a vessel of milk and gave her to drink. He was bow-legged, and she looked at his bow-leggedness and smiled, then drank and lay down to rest. He went off delighted until he came to the slave herdsman and told him the story and mentioned his joy at her smile. His companion said: "O Yasār, eat of the camel-calf's meat, drink the milk of the ten-month pregnant she-camels, and beware of the daughters of free men!" He said to him: "She laughed (daḥakat) for me a laugh I will not disappoint" — meaning ḍaḥikat lī ḍaḥkatan. Then he went to a vessel, filled it, came to his master's daughter and woke her; she drank and then lay down, and the slave sat facing her. She said: "What brought you?" He said: "What brought me is not hidden from you." She said: "What thing is it?" He said: "Your laugh (daḥkuki) that you laughed at me." She said: "May Allah greet you." Then she went to a basket of hers, took out of it incense and oil, went for a razor, called for a censer, and said to him: "Your smell is the smell of camels, and this is a fragrant oil." She placed the incense beneath him and bent down as though adjusting the incense, took hold of his genitals and cut them off with the razor; then she made him smell the oil, and slit his nose and ears, and left him. So he became proverbial for everyone who brings harm on himself and oversteps his station.
The leader of this field is Abū Tammām, for one of the most important distinguishing features of his poetry is his use of ancient and recent events, especially in his panegyrics, as in his saying in praise of Abū Dulaf:
إذا افتخرت يوما تميم بقوسها ... وزادت على ما وطّدت من مناقب
فأنتم بذي قار أمالت سيوفكم ... عروش الذين استرهنوا قوس حاجب
(If Tamīm one day boasts of its bow and adds to the merits it has established, then you at Dhū Qār — your swords toppled the thrones of those who took the bow of Ḥājib in pledge.)
He rose in his praise to mention the story of the bow of Ḥājib. Its summary is that Ḥājib ibn Zurāra, chief of Banū Tamīm, came to Chosroes in a year of drought seeking provisions. Chosroes said to him: "And what will you pledge me?" He said: "My bow." He regarded it as a great thing and gave him what he asked, and the bow of Ḥājib became proverbial among the Arabs. Then came the battle of Dhū Qār, and the Arabs defeated the Persians for the first time and liberated their land from their colonisation; the credit went to Banū Shaybān, to whom the one praised is related by lineage. So Abū Tammām said this, celebrating the mention of this event.
The discussion would become long if we traced all that has come in this field; enough of the necklace for us is what encircles the neck.
2- Hyperbole (al-mubālagha), or excess in craftsmanship (al-ifrāṭ fī al-ṣanʿa):
In His words «يكاد سنا برقه يذهب بالأبصار» there is a device which Ibn al-Muʿtazz called "excess in craftsmanship", Qudāma called "hyperbole" (al-mubālagha), and those after them called al-tablīgh; people follow Qudāma's naming. He defined it saying: "It is that the speaker mentions a state at which, had he stopped, it would have sufficed, but he does not stop at it until he adds to the meaning of his speech what is more forceful in the sense of his purpose." We have presented elsewhere in this book the kinds of hyperbole in the Mighty Book, so there is no need to repeat them. We pause at the fifth kind, to which this verse belongs, namely what runs the course of literal reality. It is of two kinds: a kind that was figurative and became literal by a contextual indication (qarīna), like this verse, for the coupling of this clause with يكاد turns it to literal reality, so it changed from impossibility to possibility; and a kind that comes in the form of the elative (ism al-tafḍīl), which is pure literal reality without any contextual indication, as in His words, Exalted is He, «أنا أكثر منك مالا وأعز نفرا» (I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in followers). The discussion of it has preceded.

dervis-irab:6-10.t:
* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أَزْواجَهُمْ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ شُهَداءُ إِلَّا أَنْفُسُهُمْ) Resumptive speech, introduced to state the rulings of liʿān (mutual imprecation), which are set out at length in the books of jurisprudence.
(الذين) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (يرمون أزواجهم) is the ṣila (relative clause). Omitting the tāʾ [i.e. using zawj rather than zawja for a wife] is more eloquent, and for that reason zawj is pluralised as azwāj; in [the law of] inheritance shares, the tāʾ must be retained. What (يرمون) is attached to is omitted, i.e. "with adultery". In (ولم) the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or a conjunction; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; (يكن) is a defective imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم); (لهم) is a fronted khabar (predicate) and (شهداء) its postponed noun; (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (أنفسهم) is a badal (substitute) of (شهداء). It is also permissible that (إلا) be in the sense of (غير), so that (أنفسهم) is an adjective (naʿt) of (شهداء), the case of (إلا) appearing on it, in the manner of His saying «لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا». (فَشَهادَةُ أَحَدِهِمْ أَرْبَعُ شَهاداتٍ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ) The fāʾ occurs in the answer to the relative noun because it contains the sense of a condition. (شهادة) is a mubtadaʾ, (أحدهم) muḍāf ilayhi, and (أربع شهادات) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The generality read (أربع) in the accusative, so the khabar of (شهادة) is either assumed to be fronted, i.e. "then upon them is the testimony", or postponed, i.e. "then the testimony of one of them is due" or "obligatory"; or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then what is obligatory is the testimony of one of them" [Translator's note: so in the source; the reading of Ḥafṣ, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, as printed here, has (أربعُ) in the nominative, and the source parsed it as the khabar just above]. As for the accusative of (أربع), it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), governed by a maṣdar like it, its number having substituted for the maṣdar. (بالله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (شهادات) or to (شهادة), so the question belongs to the topic of tanāzuʿ (two governors competing for one governed word). Inna and its noun; the hamza of inna is given kasra because of the presence of the lām; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (من الصادقين) is the khabar of inna. Inna and what follows it are the object of (شهادات) or (شهادة), i.e. he testifies that he is truthful. The clause (فشهادة أحدهم) is the khabar of (الذين).
(وَالْخامِسَةُ أَنَّ لَعْنَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ إِنْ كانَ مِنَ الْكاذِبِينَ) The wāw is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya); (الخامسة) is a mubtadaʾ, i.e. the fifth testimony; (أن) and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar that is the khabar; (لعنة الله) is the noun of (أن) and (عليه) the khabar of (أن). (إن) is conditional; (كان) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the noun of kāna is latent (mustatir); (من الكاذبين) is the khabar of kāna; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. It is also permissible that the wāw be a conjunction and (الخامسة) be conjoined to (شهادة), with (أن لعنة الله) a badal of (الخامسة), or accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "that the curse of Allah…"; the first is easier. (وَيَدْرَؤُا عَنْهَا الْعَذابَ أَنْ تَشْهَدَ أَرْبَعَ شَهاداتٍ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الْكاذِبِينَ) The clause (ويدرأ) is conjoined to what precedes. (يدرأ) is an imperfect verb meaning "averts"; (عنها) is attached to it; (العذاب) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أن تشهد) is interpreted as a maṣdar that is the fāʿil (agent) of (يدرأ); (أربع شهادات) is accusative as a maṣdar, so it is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); (بالله) is attached to (شهادات) or to (أن تشهد), as preceded in the first; and the i'rab of (إنه لمن الكاذبين) has preceded. (وَالْخامِسَةَ أَنَّ غَضَبَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْها إِنْ كانَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ) The i'rab of its like has preceded, so refresh your memory of it. (وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ حَكِيمٌ) (لولا) is a particle of impossibility because of existence (imtināʿ li-wujūd); (فضل الله) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is necessarily omitted, as preceded; (عليكم) is attached to (فضل); (رحمته) is conjoined to (فضل); (أن الله تواب) is anna, its noun and its khabar, and it is conjoined to (فضل). The apodosis of (لولا) is omitted, as an indication of an omitted matter whose essence cannot be grasped because of its magnitude and gravity; and many a thing passed over in silence is more eloquent than what is uttered.

* Rhetoric:
In addition to the rulings and sound legislation they contain, these verses comprise numerous rhetorical devices. They have been discussed before, so we shall content ourselves with pointing to them:
1- Iltifāt (shift of person): in His saying «ولولا فضل الله عليكم» He shifted from the third person to the second, to record the favour upon those addressed, so that no flimsy excuses remain with them to cling to if they transgress the limits He has made clear to them.
2- Taghlīb (giving precedence): He gave the masculine form precedence over the feminine form, in that He did not say "upon you (masc.) and upon you (fem.)", because He is addressing both parties, i.e. the slandering men and the slandered women.
3- Ḥadhf (omission): the omission of the mubtadaʾ and the khabar has recurred, as you saw in the i'rab, and the apodosis of (لولا) has been omitted, i.e. as if Allah were to say in His exposition: so-and-so is truthful about the adultery, because the slandered woman did in reality commit adultery; or to say: so-and-so is lying in his slander, because the slandered woman did not in reality commit adultery. He drew the curtain over all that because the highest aim is protection [of honour]; protection demands caution, and caution calls for silence about what it is not good to state openly.
